Alipay-PIBench: Payment Integration Benchmark for Coding Agents (Ying / Cao / Ma / Dong / Chen / Song / Zhu) — 9 product-specific projects x 18 task instances organized into Basic (functional-completion) + Advanced (risk-aware hardening) tiers; deterministic static + unit + integration + E2E checks with LLM-assisted semantic assessment; evaluated 6 coding-agent models; mean RPR 68.58->91.37% with skill access; access to Alipay payment integration skills improved mean RPR by average +10.31pp; fifth skill-package-unlocks-bounded-domain-performance data point

Welcome Inkling by Thinking Machines (Burtenshaw, Merve, Cuenca, Roy Gosthipaty — HF launch post; Thinking Machines model) — open-source multimodal decoder-only MoE, 975B total / 41B active, 66 layers, 256 experts, hybrid attention (5:1 sliding-window : global), short conv + relative attention, 1M-token context, trained on 45T tokens across text+image+audio; Apache 2.0; day-one Transformers/SGLang/vLLM/TokenSpeed/Unsloth support with NVFP4 variant and 1-bit GGUF via Unsloth (UD-IQ1_S) at launch (retains ~74.2% of top-1% accuracy at ~86% smaller); benchmarks — SWE-Bench Verified 77.6%, SWE-Bench Pro Public 54.3%, AIME 2026 97.1%, GPQA Diamond 87.2%, MMMU Pro 73.3%, Charxiv RQ 78.1%, VoiceBench 91.4%, Global-MMLU-Lite 88.7%; first natively-audio ~1T-scale open-weight release

Oracle Agent Memory as an Enterprise Memory Substrate for Long-Horizon AI Agents (Alake, Bernardis, Cayet, Engel, Hilloulin, Hong, Hosler, Kavantzas, Kossyk, Le, Patra, Talamadupula, Venzin — Oracle) — database-native memory system on Oracle Database with full lifecycle (ingestion / extraction / consolidation / retrieval / removal), layered active-vs-passive architecture with explicit scope controls, evaluated by task accuracy + memory-specific metrics (retrieval quality, latency); 93.8% LongMemEval accuracy at ~10.7x fewer tokens than flat-history baselines; joins Shared Selective Persistent Memory (2607.09493) and MemOps (2607.12893) as third memory paper in 48 hours flipping the naive full-history default; over-context penalty primitive

Memory as a Controlled Process: Learned Adaptive Memory Management for LLM Agents / MemCon (Eric Hanchen Jiang, Zhi Zhang, Yuchen Wu, Levina Li, Dong Liu, Xiao Liang, Rui Sun, Yubei Li, Edward Sun, Haozheng Luo, Zhaolu Kang, Aylin Caliskan, Kai-Wei Chang, Ying Nian Wu — UCLA + collaborators) — models memory operations (retrieve/inject/consolidate) as MDP; learns per-context policy via lightweight tabular contextual bandit with UCB exploration; task-level binary feedback only, no LLM in policy loop, converges within tens of tasks across memory backends; +15.2pp task success and 5-20% token reduction across 6 benchmarks x 3 agent frameworks x 3 backbones; first Pareto win (accuracy up AND tokens down) with a memory policy learner light enough for MCP loops; refutes implicit mem0/LangMem/Letta assumption that memory policies need an LLM

Experience Memory Graph: One-Shot Error Correction for Agents (Wenjun Wang, Yuchen Fang, Fengrui Liu, Zibo Liang, Kai Zheng) — converts failed AND successful trajectories into directed action decision graphs; mines common successful workflows; derives graph-edit paths (action add/delete/relabel) transforming failing trajectory into successful one; at inference graph-match against memory graph and apply edit path — single-pass, no reflection loop; beats reflection baselines on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld on success rate and average reward with zero test-time trial-and-error; reframes error recovery as graph matching over trajectory memory instead of prompt-based critique-retry

Adaptive Filtering of the KV Cache: Diagnosing and Correcting Structural-Role Bias in LLM Inference (Soumil Mandal) — diagnoses H2O and other attention-mass eviction policies over-retain structural KEY tokens (delimiters, whitespace, JSON braces) at ~1.8x the rate of answer-carrying VALUE tokens; on schema-dense inputs H2O accuracy collapses from 88% -> 0% at 5% memory budget; fix is a 15 MB linear probe that role-classifies tokens (KEY/VALUE/sink) and applies role-conditional retention on top of SnapKV-style windowed scoring; retraining-free, single hyperparameter, recovers 63-98% of accuracy loss; direct silent-failure diagnosis for long-context tool-response distributions (MCP JSON)

Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0 (Wenxiao Wang, Priyatham Kattakinda, Soheil Feizi — RELAI) — two-phase continual-learning evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0 comparing GEPA / Meta Harness / RELAI-VCL at identical optimization budgets with re-optimization on newly-introduced tasks in phase two; RELAI-VCL 76.4% lifelong pass, GEPA 66.0%, Meta Harness 64.6%, unoptimized baseline 58.7%; load-bearing finding: optimization gains compound ONLY when regression control is built into the optimization loop; optimizers without regression control get shortcut-solved and undo their own prior wins; direct extension of Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench (2607.08964) thread with a lifelong framing; fourth gate-before-commit datapoint of the month

Self-Evolving Agent Harnesses via Gated Semantic Quality-Diversity (Xiaotian Luo, Fengxingyu Wang, Chuanrui Hu, Dizhan Xue, Yafeng Deng) — automated agent-harness improvement (prompts / knowledge / runtime control / config, no weight updates) that separates change proposal from change crediting; LLM diagnoses failures + proposes patches, deterministic code measures whether patch helps under significance testing; quality-diversity archive keyed on failure pathology (WHERE x WHY) rather than task — anti-overfitting inductive bias; +9 to +15.5pp on training domains, 86-147% of that gain retained on sealed test set (>100% retention indicates pathology-keyed patches generalize better than they train); pathology > task as design principle; third harness-evolution paper in-window

Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable, Navigable, and Editable (Ruhan Wang, Yucheng Shi, Zongxia Li, Zhongzhi Li, Yue Yu, Junyao Yang, Kishan Panaganti, Haitao Mi, Dongruo Zhou, Leoweiliang) — behavior-centric map of agent harness auto-synthesized via static analysis + LLM structuring linking each observable behavior to source-code sites that implement it; paired with Behavior-Guided Progressive Disclosure (BGPD) — navigation policy starting from target behavior and progressively surfacing implementation details while validating candidate edit sites against current source before committing; evaluated on modification requests across two open-source harnesses; Handbook-Assisted improves behavior localization and edit-plan quality using fewer planner tokens, largest gains on scattered sites, rarely executed paths, and cross-module interactions; addresses the pre-optimization step (where to edit) that no prior harness-evolution work instrumented

AgentCompass: A Unified Evaluation Infrastructure for Agent Capabilities (Zichen Ding + 22 co-authors) — open-source lightweight extensible infrastructure for evaluating LLM-based agents; decouples evaluation into three independent components (Benchmark / Harness / Environment) enabling flexible configurations; asynchronous fault-tolerant runtime, trajectory analysis tools for diagnosing failure modes including reward-hacking; supports 20+ benchmarks across five capability dimensions; released CC BY 4.0; first open-source infra spanning the current benchmark cluster (Terminal-Bench 2.0, tau-bench, OSWorld, etc.) instead of hand-rolled per-suite runners

PM-Bench: Evaluating Prospective Memory in LLM Agents (Genglin Liu, Saadia Gabriel — COLM 2026) — first LLM adaptation of cognitive science Virtual Week paradigm testing deferred-intent execution over a simulated 7-day horizon across 8 frontier LLMs and varied memory strategies (no-memory / scratchpad / structured episodic / retrieval); best system 65.1% F1 leaving >30% gap; no single memory strategy dominates across models — plug-and-play mem0 wrappers insufficient; new time-deferred dimension extending memory-benchmark cluster (LoCoMo, LongMemEval, Mem-Gallery)

MemOps: Benchmarking Lifecycle Memory Operations in Long-Horizon Conversations (Xixuan Hao, Zeyu Zhang, Zehao Lin) — reframes conversational memory as sequence of lifecycle operations (remember / forget / update / reflect) with structured traces (trigger, target, scope, state transitions, evidence); six operation-level probe categories under adjacent-evidence and long-context settings; session-level retrieval beats turn-level; long-context models struggle to reconstruct ordered memory-state trajectories; moves eval from final-answer scoring to interpretable operation-level diagnosis

Shared Selective Persistent Memory for Agentic LLM Systems (Sanjana Pedada, Aditya Dhavala, Neelraj Patil) — retains four reusable categories (task specs, data schemas, tool configs, output constraints) while discarding session-specific reasoning traces; role-based access, git-versioned artifacts, zero-token refresh mechanism; 96% task completion vs 79% no-memory vs 71% full-history (over-context penalty first-class evidence); 14x task-time reduction from zero-token refresh, 97x per-invocation token savings vs raw data injection, 12/12 zero-token refresh trials

A JoLT for the KV Cache: Near-Lossless KV Cache Compression via Joint Tucker and JL-Residual Allocation (Rahul Krishnan, Volker Schulz) — treats KV cache as third-order tensor with partial Tucker decomposition on token/feature axes + JL-rotated low-bit residual for truncated energy; one Lagrangian dual jointly allocates Tucker ranks + residual bit-widths per layer group, separately for K and V, under single byte budget; FlashJoLT kernel 5-13x faster to compress; 2-3x near-lossless KV compression on Mistral-7B-v0.3 and LLaMA-2-13B; Frobenius error 0.009 (K) / 0.006 (V) at 2x (order of magnitude below cross-layer SVD and 4-bit quant baselines); perplexity/GSM8K/RULER preserved; 9,125 tok/s throughput

StructAgent: Harness Long-horizon Digital Agents with Unified Causal Structure (Wenyi Wu, Sibo Zhu, Kun Zhou) — state-centered computer-use framework replacing raw interaction history with compact verifiable task-progress state + structured workflow of verifier-backed transitions; explicit progress checkpointing, evidence-driven completion, targeted failure recovery; OSWorld-Verified Qwen3.5-9B 27.0->46.9%, Qwen3.5-27B 31.6->62.2%, MiniMax-M3 78.9% new open-source SOTA; wrapper matters more than backbone swap; eleventh convergent gate-before-commit instance in the vault

Speculate with Memory: Lossless Acceleration for LLM Agents (Yu Li, Qinyuan Ye, Prafulla Kumar Choubey) — turns stateless speculator into memory-augmented predictor with three online stores (contrastive transition table for action-sequence statistics + episodic memory for similar past segments + confusion tracker suppressing recurring mistakes); all speculation runs during environment idle time so wall-clock-free and lossless; 19-39% relative action-prediction accuracy gain, up to 2.5x on observation prediction in repetitive action spaces, six benchmarks; gains grow monotonically with accumulated memory

Function-Aware Fill-in-the-Middle Mid-Training for Coding Agents (Yubo Wang, Jiarong Liang, Yuxuan Zhang) — action-observation-continuation loop isomorphic to function call site; self-supervised FIM objective masks functions selected by program-dependency-graph analysis under complexity-inferability criterion; mid-trains on 2.6B decontaminated tokens from 968 GitHub repos; SWE-Bench-Verified +2.8/+3.0/+3.2 on Qwen2.5-Coder 7B/14B and Qwen3-8B; SWE-Bench-Lite +3.7/+4.0/+5.4; also mitigates capability erosion from agentic post-training on LiveCodeBench, tau-bench, BFCL (rare evidence collateral damage is addressable not intrinsic)

How to Run an Autoresearch Workflow with RL Agent Skills and NVIDIA NeMo (NVIDIA Nemotron / NeMo team, 2026-07-14) — durable ML-research loop with agent skills (Brev-etiquette, session-memory, autoresearch) encoding ops context + reusable procedures; Codex (GPT-5.5) orchestrates setup / experiments / paper-to-code; NeMo RL + NeMo Gym for VLM training; Qwen3-VL-2B improved 25%->96.9% on custom visual-counting task; OAPL algorithm beat DAPO baselines on math reasoning; applied convergence of skill-as-first-class-artifact + long-running autonomous loop + coding-agent-managed-ML-experiment themes

ABot-AgentOS: A General Robotic Agent OS with Lifelong Multi-modal Memory (Tian et al., 24+ authors — Alibaba AMAP CV Lab) — agent OS with scene-conditioned planning + lifelong multi-modal memory + verification + cross-embodiment execution; LoCoMo 88.7 / OpenEQA EM-EQA 60.4 / Mem-Gallery 89.0 / NExT-QA 76.5 with self-evolution; ships executable EmbodiedWorldBench (16 scenes, 200+ tasks); code released; small self-evolution delta (+1.2 / +0.5 / +0.4) suggests memory benches near saturation, self-evolution is now the interesting axis; direct memory-and-orchestration reference decomposition for MCP-tool agents

LightMem-Ego: Your AI Memory for Everyday Life (Chen, Xiao, Zhao, Xia, Xu, Fang, Li, Zheng, Wang, Xue, Zhang, Li, Ningyu Zhang — ZJUNLP) — personal AI memory for continuous egocentric visual+audio streams from mobile/wearable; hierarchical memory levels + selective retrieval; supports object-finding, conversation recall, life summarization, routine discovery, personalized assistance; direct on-device / M5-Max architecture transplant; realizes Always-On Agents thesis on egocentric device profile; ongoing work — code released, no headline benchmark numbers yet

Agentic Context Learning with Self-Discovered Specification / PSCI (Zhong, Li, Lai, Yang, Xie, Kil, Mai, Lo, Xiang, Psounis, Lei) — 55.4% of CL-Bench rubric items evaluate specification acquisition vs 22.6% content acquisition; frontier <24% baseline; PSCI (Private Specification-Contract Induction) extracts task specifications as first-class contracts; GPT-5.1 28.14% (+5.59 pp / +24.8% relative), Qwen3.5-27B +5.28 pp, Gemini 3 Pro +6.17 pp; specification-vs-content dichotomy is load-bearing framing insight (~2.5:1 spec-to-content ratio, empirical); shared primitive with Self-Guided TTT [arxiv:2607.09415] and Rate-Distortion Compaction [arxiv:2607.08032]

AgentAbstain: Do LLM Agents Know When Not to Act? (Liu, Y.E. Zhang, Kasprova, Rabbani, Zahraei, T. Zhang, Ebrahimpour-Boroojeny, Chandrasekaran) — 263 paired should-act/should-abstain tasks x 8 abstention scenarios x 42 sandbox environments; best model Gemini 3.1 Pro only 59.5% paired accuracy; abstention capability largely independent of general task-solving capability (not scale-emergent); names post-hoc abstention failure mode (irreversible action executed before abstention trigger recognized); ships AbstainGen automated regeneration pipeline for contamination resistance; 94-98% rated well-designed; third abstention-first benchmark in 5 days ([arxiv:2607.08456] 07-10, [arxiv:2607.08093] 07-13, this 07-14)

EvoCUA-1.5: Online Reinforcement Learning for Multi-turn Computer-Use Agents (Huang, Xue, Peng, Ding, Fan, Hong, Gao, X. Zhang, Guo, Yang, Zhao, Xie, Pei, X. Xie, Qiu) — Step-Level Policy Optimization (STEPO) + policy-aware trajectory filtering + Dynamic Tri-Adaptive Curriculum (DTAC) + async RL infra; addresses context-managed observations, sparse terminal rewards, variable-length trajectories, slow environment feedback; 63.2% OSWorld-Verified beats 32B/35B-scale open baselines with smaller model; online-RL half-recipe of open CUA training cluster (pairs with OpenWebRL browser side, CUA-Gym env side, LearnWeak specialization, UI-MOPD multi-platform, Autonomous-Eval reward-noise correction); base-model size not specified in abstract

Who&When Pro: Can LLMs Really Attribute Failures in AI Agents? (Liu, Xi, S. Zhang, Zeng, Yue, Wang, Kang, Wu, H. Wang) — 12,326 failed agent trajectories across 3 modalities x 26 benchmarks; controlled failure-injection pipeline after successful prefixes for golden-label attribution; systematic patterns across modalities/protocols/model families; attribution capability tracks separately from general task-solving; frames as agents become more capable failures get subtler — attribution on critical path for production reliability; direct upstream requirement for DeepMind AI Control Roadmap trusted-monitor architecture and Workflow-GYM four-failure-mode taxonomy

Length Penalties Make Chain-of-Thought Less Monitorable (Bryce Little) — length-penalized RL preserves accuracy but preferentially removes influence-disclosure tokens monitors need; Qwen3-14B hint-detection 69%->49%, Qwen3-4B 60%->48%; lower-bound faithfulness drops to 63.1% and 69.4% of baseline; compressed chains disclose hints 7-35 pp less than random-shortened chains (directed removal, not just shorter); 5 evaluation distributions (MMLU-Pro-R + 4 transfer benchmarks); third data point (after DiffusionGemma 28.6x opacity + Unfaithful Capitulation) that cheaper/more capable/more compact reasoning erodes CoT monitorability; direct tension with DeepMind AI Control Roadmap monitor-on-CoT bet

Dynamic Agent Skills: A Lifecycle Survey and Taxonomy of Evolving Skill Libraries (Yubo Li — TMLR 2026) — survey of 124 papers (2023-2026) organized around 8-stage skill lifecycle: evidence collection -> skill proposal -> verification/admission -> storage -> retrieval/composition -> maintenance -> distillation/portability -> governance; skills broadly defined (code, NL instructions, packages, workflow graphs, adapters); recurring empirical findings: admission and repair repeatedly important, verifier quality materially affects skill-aware RL, flat retrieval degrades as libraries grow, benchmarks under-cover library trajectories and safety; first shared vocabulary for the skill-management primitive that Mistral Studio / Codex Record & Replay / Claude Tag / SkillOpt have been building without common taxonomy

Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench: Testing the Limits of Agents on Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks with Dense Reward-Based Grading (Tencent Hunyuan) — 46 tasks x 9 categories with dense per-checkpoint partial credit; frontier best 15.2% at high reward threshold, all-model average 4.3%; average ~10M tokens + ~85 minutes wall-clock per task; dense-reward instrumentation extension of Terminal-Bench 2.0 line

Self-Guided Test-Time Training for Long-Context LLMs (Zhu, Xu, Wei, Pu, Tian, Sun, Rangadurai, Zhi, Shyu, Pandey, Simon, Meng, Liu) — TTT on random spans HURTS LongBench-v2 accuracy while TTT on oracle spans substantially helps; Self-Guided TTT has the model identify evidence spans before applying LM-loss training on those spans only; up to 15% relative improvement on Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on LongBench-v2 + LongBench-Pro; span-quality-sensitivity is the load-bearing insight; direct M5-Max local-fit

Soofi S 30B-A3B: A Sovereign, Open-Source Foundation Model for German and English (Soofi-Team, 30 members: Droste, Fitzek, Haerle, Frey, Gurgurov, Luebbering et al. — German Industrial AI Cloud / Deutsche Telekom) — sovereign fully-open MoE hybrid Mamba-Transformer, 30B/3B-A, ~27T tokens with German upweighting; matches dense 14-27B on combined DE-EN, highest English AND German scores among fully-open models beating Olmo 3 32B and Apertus 70B; permissive open-access with weights + checkpoints + training code + data docs; third fully-open hybrid-Mamba MoE (after Nemotron 3 Ultra + Agents-A1); direct M5-Max local-fit

WILDTRACE: Benchmarking Natural Evidence Trails in Long-Context Reasoning (Chen, Liu, Li, Sheng, Tu, Deng, Huang, Shum, Liu, Qu) — 481 tasks from 214 real long-form sources (technical incident reports + literary narratives); all evidence trails arise from the document's own causal/temporal/narrative logic (not planted needles); seven distinct evidence patterns under Pearl's causal hierarchy; explicit companion to PredicateLongBench (arxiv:2607.08284) + Jet-Long (arxiv:2607.07740) in the naturalistic long-context benchmark cluster

Towards Mechanistically Understanding Why Memorized Knowledge Fails to Generalize in Large Language Model Finetuning / Knowing-Using Gap (Dai, Rao, Wang, Wang, Liu, Xiong — HKUST) — self-patching to track memorized representations through model layers; memorized reps can exist internally but fail to route to computation-effective layers (knowledge-circuit misalignment); diagnostic strategy recovers 58-75% of the generalization gap in failure cases; explains SFT-recall-vs-usage divergence

Linear Attention Architectures: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Cross-Layer Routing (Cerruti, Rieder, Rowlands, Jin, Schlag — ETH Zurich) — head-to-head DeltaNet / Gated DeltaNet / Kimi Delta Attention / Gated DeltaNet-2 under shared notation at 350M-3B on 15B tokens; Kimi Delta Attention + Muon wins validation loss, Gated DeltaNet + AdamW wins throughput; introduces Cross-Layer Value Routing (CLVR) — forwarding the write value across layers — as lightweight routing signal lowering final validation loss for both DeltaNet and Gated DeltaNet

CausalDS: Benchmarking Causal Reasoning in Data-Science Agents (Leban, Sun — University of Michigan) — bridges symbolic-causal-benches-without-data + data-benches-without-causal-structure gap; each instance ships a structural causal model + observational data + grounded natural-language narrative + empirically-informed real distributions; covers all three Pearl levels; abstention (recognizing an unanswerable question) as first-class scored outcome; jointly evaluates symbolic causal reasoning + data science + uncertainty quantification + abstention + tool-use/coding; second reference-benchmark this month scoring abstention (after Two Axes of Abstention arxiv:2607.08456)

What to Keep, What to Forget: A Rate-Distortion View of Memory Compaction in LLMs and Agents (Colaco, Lahjouji) — unifies KV cache management + prompt pruning + architectural state bounding + agent memory consolidation as one rate-distortion problem; names attention-magnitude/recency as universal failure mode; measurement-gap flag: repeated compaction that agents actually perform is almost never measured; taxonomy + benchmarking-protocol contribution; theoretical spine for memory cluster (Memora/AutoMem/Janus/MemDelta/A-TMA/CanonicalMerge/SelfMem)

Persuasion Attacks Can Decrease Effectiveness of CoT Monitoring (Za, Bainiaksina, Ostrovsky, Chopra, Krakovna @ Google DeepMind) — monitor access to agent CoT INCREASES approval of harmful actions by 9.5% (persuasion channel); 40 policy-violating proposal tasks; fix — model-diverse fact-checker (Claude 3.7 Sonnet monitor + GPT-4.1 fact-checker) cuts harmful approvals 45% vs 6% same-family; refutes CoT-monitoring-as-safety default

When LLMs Agree, Are They Right? Auditing Self-Consistency and Cross-Model Agreement (Ding) — 265K samples x 53 runners on GPQA Diamond + AIME; agreement is positive but weak predictor r=0.20-0.59; frontier models 77% agreement / ~half wrong on GPQA; agreement performs best for mid-tier unsaturated models, fails for frontier; self-consistency is conditional proxy for correctness not standalone confidence score; fourth convergent refutation of within-family agreement metric (Blind Curator + Huang null + LLM-as-Judge Reliability + this)

Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution (Leung, Lumer, Feld, Huber, Subbiah, Paul) — 8 judges x 1248 rubric decisions incl 378 hard cases from judge disagreements; two dims: source relevance + factual support; GPT-5-mini strongest source-relevance pass-class F1 0.908; warning: scalar F1 obscures directional bias exactly what downstream RL loop would reinforce; cheap-judge sufficient at inference time / dangerous as RL reward signal

Hidden Decoding at Scale: Latent Computation Scaling for Large Language Models (Aiwei Liu + 46 co-authors, WeLM team) — per-token latent computation scaling; expands each token into n independent streams with separate embedding tables + KV caching; Stream-Factorized Attention keeps mostly linear cost; validated at WeLM-HD4-80B and WeLM-HD4-617B with n=4; first successful sequence-width scaling demo at 100B+ MoE scale; expand-frozen-model architectural extension (companion to HiLS-Attention arxiv:2607.02980 + Frozen MTP google-research-2026-06-26)

It Takes a MAESTRO To Prune Bad Experts (Goel, Maheshwari, Chakraborty) — models autoregressive expert activation trajectories as Ergodic Markov chains with stationary distributions encoding cross-layer dependencies; globally-aware routing importance metric replaces local heuristics; at 50% compression outperforms SOTA baselines by up to 10.61% average performance retention across Safety/Bias/Ethics; substantially lower cross-task variance; direct M5-Max local-fit for Qwen3.6-A3B / Gemma 4-A4B / Leanstral 6B-A when llama.cpp or MLX PR lands

Game Theory Driven Multi-Agent Framework Mitigates LLM Hallucination / G-Frame -> OmniChem (Liu, Bie, Wang, Ma, Yexin Liu, Li, Yang, Yang, Cao, Tao) — Bayesian + team-game closed-loop for data synthesis + training; 363,045 CoTs + 199,589 QA pairs synthesized; OmniChem 7B matches GPT-4o-mini on custom + ChemBench; 79.46% hallucination reduction vs base; chemistry domain evidence but training-protocol contribution domain-generic; needs cross-domain reproduction

Mistral Studio — Prompts and Skills as System of Record (Mistral AI, 2026-07-09) — versioned prompt + skill management with immutable versions (a version that shipped cant be quietly changed), rollback with diff, named ownership, classification labels (Production/Staging), audit logs of every change (who + when), skills exposed as MCP servers from Studio so production execution matches governed version; productizes seven-instance gate-before-commit / provenance-tracking cluster (Janus/SkillOpt/Mnemosyne/RoPoLL+Minority Sentinel/ProvenanceGuard/ContextNest/Reason-Less-Verify-More + arxiv:2607.08028 From Prompts to Contracts)

Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents (Meta) — proactive memory agent runs alongside action agent + selectively injects context reminders to prevent behavioral state decay; Qwen3.5-27B memory agent trained via SFT+GRPO on SETA; Terminal-Bench 2.0 pass@1 +8.3 pp, tau^2-Bench pass@1 +6.8 pp; beats passive retrieval + continuous injection + advisor-only + general RAG; plug-and-play with frontier action agents; CC BY 4.0; memory-as-interventionist thesis vs memory-as-store

KronQ: LLM Quantization via Kronecker-Factored Hessian (COLM 2026) — post-training weight-only quantization; Kronecker-factored Hessian + gradient covariance + bidirectional incoherence + gradient-informed mixed-precision allocation; 2-bit LLaMA-3-70B WikiText-2 PPL 7.93 vs GPTQ/GPTAQ >2000 at same 2-bit budget; makes 70B usable-quality on M5 Max 64 GB with ~18-20 GB weights + KV headroom

From Prompts to Contracts: Harness Engineering for Auditable Enterprise LLM Agents — moves behavioral enforcement from prompts into code + manifests + validators; contract taxonomy: source-grounding/entity-routing/trace/output-hygiene/recommendation; 3-model substitution (270 runs) isolates failures to model-composed layer; head-to-head: prompt-only permits safety violations, bolt-on guardrail over-refuses (88/120 utility), harness scores 120/120 utility with zero safety violations; deployment-time complement to Reason-Less-Verify-More (arxiv:2607.07405)

AgentLocate: Who Broke the System? Failure Localization in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems (COLM 2026) — LLM judge + independent evaluators + confidence-weighted aggregation + adaptive fine-tuning; identifies BOTH responsible agent AND earliest decisive step; beats prior failure-localization methods on two benchmarks with lower token cost + wall-clock; missing root-cause primitive for autonomous multi-subagent loops

WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search (RUC + Kwai) — first probes how information is organized on web to seed fan-out; dynamically instantiates child search nodes with per-node objective + search mode; reuses process-level experience across homogeneous sibling nodes; consistently beats single-agent + prior multi-agent baselines on BrowseComp-Plus, WideSearch, DeepWideSearch, GISA; sibling process-trace reuse is the load-bearing primitive

PredicateLongBench: Understanding Axes of Difficulty For Long Context Tasks — conceptually simple LLM-judge-free task (find longest contiguous subsequence satisfying a predicate like lexicographic ordering); both synthetic and natural-document-preserving pipelines; explicit difficulty axes (titratable, not one scalar); frontier models degrade cleanly as difficulty scales along axes; anti-saturation benchmark long-context has been missing; natural pairing with Jet-Long (arxiv:2607.07740); CC BY 4.0

DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding — training-free; tree-drafting + Domino GRU causal correction; Qwen3-4B up to 6.6x speedup vs autoregressive; mean accept length 10.7 tokens/round (highest of any evaluated method); +9-10% throughput over Domino decoder overall, +22% on Alpaca; +24% over DDTree/CaDDTree at T=0 on Qwen3-8B; GitHub repo confirmed; 8 benchmarks across temperatures; direct M5 Max local-fit

Jet-Long: Efficient Long-Context Extension with Dynamic Bifocal RoPE (NVIDIA) — tuning-free zero-shot; Qwen3 1.7B/4B/8B up to 128K beats RULER by +4.79/+2.18/+2.03 pts; 1.39x FA2 prefill throughput on H100; <=4% single-batch overhead at every length; wins HELMET-RAG; wins PG-19 perplexity; generalizes to hybrid attention (Jet-Nemotron) without retraining; direct M5-Max Qwen3-8B fit

Tool-Making and Self-Evolving LLM Agents in Low-Latency Systems — production tool-making pipeline compiles repeated SOP steps into validated versioned tools before deployment; 44-node fulfillment-center alarm-triage workflow, 1,500 historical alarms; p50 latency -42%; end-to-end error rate down up to 53% (variance elimination); further -62% p50 latency in direct-call ablation; versioned tools expose spec gaps + data drift as a signal

From Atomic Actions to Standard Operating Procedures / EvoSOP — same-day companion to arxiv:2607.08010; formalizes SOP-compilation as construct/merge/evaluate/prune cycles over an SOP library extracted from execution traces; reports task success rate + interaction round efficiency gains vs baseline (no headline number)

UniClawBench: Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks (HKU-MMLab) — 400 bilingual live-Docker tasks across 5 competencies (skill usage, exploration, long-context, multimodal, cross-platform coordination); closed-loop with executor + hidden supervisor + user simulator; grading criteria hidden from agent; headline: base capability x harness design jointly determine performance; github.com/HKU-MMLab/UniClawBench

LLM-as-Judge Reliability Auditing — Qwen3 dense 1.7B->32B + MiniMax M2->M2.7; only Qwen3 1.7B->4B produces robust adjacent improvements; larger judges reduce but do not eliminate position/verbosity bias; repeated-sample juries minimal value when errors correlate (matches arxiv:2607.05904 55%-hacked-accepted); structured debate can shift decisions but requires parser + fallback logs; recommends dataset slices + bias probes + error-dependence estimates + protocol audit trails

Two Axes of LLM Abstention (Wagner) — answer confidence and question answerability are independent axes; 5 instruction-tuned models 2B-14B, 3 families; CREPE false-premise: answer-confidence + P(IK) + P(True) + direct-premise-check all near chance, hidden-state probe 0.69-0.77 AUROC; direct instruction to check premises = 57% false challenges; probe routing triples challenge precision; two-axis policy certifies 0.75 correct-answer coverage vs 0.31 for single-threshold; at 14B two-axis policy is the only one that certifies at all

Hallucination Self-Play / HSP (COLM 2026) — two roles from same base model: detector fine-tuned on human labels + generator trained via RLAIF using detector as reward model; evolved generator produces harder-to-detect hallucinations then feeds rule-based RL to sharpen detector; RAGTruth: small LLM matches or beats advanced LLM detector without external supervision; escapes arxiv:2607.05904 self-play-reward-hacking pathology because one side is anchored to human labels and one side uses rule-based RL (asymmetric grounding)

DeepSearch-Evolve / DeepSearch-World — deterministic verifiable environment with reproducible search + page-reading; 420K multi-hop QA from entity-level random walks; iterative self-distillation loop (trajectory gen -> filter -> mix -> fine-tune) with no external teacher; 9B parameter model: BrowseComp 31.2 / GAIA 61.5 / HotpotQA 93.4; validates 'verifiable environment > teacher model' thesis for long-horizon web agents at local-inference-relevant model size

Reason Less, Verify More: Deterministic Gates Recover a Silent Policy-Violation Failure Mode in Tool-Using LLM Agents — read-only pre-execution gates on tau2-bench airline (50 tasks); gpt-4o-mini 29.6->42.0% (+12.4pp, P=0.0012); gpt-5.2 61.2->71.6% (+10.4pp); firing tasks +19.2pp; negative controls (BFCL, tau2 retail) confirm gates add nothing where tools already self-enforce; 9th convergent instance of gate-before-commit lineage; execution-time analog of yesterday's commit-first fix at eval time

Do LLM-Generated Skills Make Better AI Data Scientists? A Component Ablation Across Data-Science Workflows — 56 tasks x 9 configs x 3 providers = 7,560 runs + 1,512-run control study; NO reliable improvement from any skill variant; total spread 1.2pp across all variants; all p >= 0.396; falsifies default single-shot prompting via LLM-generated skills for data-science workflows; direct COMPARE against SkillOpt (Microsoft, +23.5pp GPT-5.5) and SkillOpt-Lite (LMMs-Lab, GPT-5.4-nano beats GPT-5.5 baseline)

The Blind Curator: How a Biased Judge Silently Disables Skill Retirement in Self-Evolving Agents — false-pass bias is NOT additional noise; it categorically switches off contribution-based retirement past a sharp threshold that no amount of data can cross; universal across domains and failure rates; surfaces in NO aggregate metric; proposes cheap defect-injection audit (inject known-bad candidates and check false-pass rate) to predict which side of the threshold a deployed judge occupies before deployment; mechanism-side sequel to yesterday's Self-Play Reward Hacking

Cost-Effective Agent Harnesses for Abstract Reasoning and Generalization on ARC-AGI-1 — Explorer-Definer + Reflective Orchestrator on DeepSeek V3.2 without ARC-specific training; baseline one-shot 15.5% pass@2 -> pipeline alone 57.5% ($0.25/task) -> pipeline + Reflective Orchestrator 67.25% pass@2 at $0.62/task; Orchestrator adds +9.81pp on pass@1; central architectural claim: pipeline is generation-bound not selection-bound (broader adaptive re-exploration helps; better ranking does not)

When Agents Remember Too Much: Memory Poisoning Attacks on Large Language Model Agents (GhostWriter) — two-phase attack on personal-assistant agents (conversational + action planning + long-term memory); Phase 1 injection ~98% success rate (poison lands in memory store); Phase 2 activation ~60% success rate (fires downstream on retrieval and influences action); AM-Sentry defense proposed (memory-saving policies + retrieval screening); dramatically reduces success while preserving utility; direct adversarial pressure on memory-injection cluster (Memora / AutoMem / SelfMem / DynaKRAG / A-TMA)

The Harness Effect: How Orchestration Design Sets the Token Economics of Enterprise Agentic AI — six-model controlled study (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1, Gemini Flash 3.5, Qwen 3.6, GLM 5.1, Palmyra X6) x 22 locked tasks; Writer Agent Harness vs conventional production baseline; cost per task $0.21 -> $0.12 (-41%); tokens per task 14,200 -> 8,800 (-38%); wall-clock 48s -> 27s (-44%); quality 0.78 -> 0.81 (slightly up); first clean isolation of orchestration variable at six-model scale; gains hold across ALL six models

Search, Fail, Recover: A Training Framework for Correction-Aware Reasoning (Pyligent) — trains models on continue/finish/backtrack actions using task validator to label BOTH successful continuations AND failed branches; hidden directed-graph task +72.7pp over gold-only SFT; 4x4 Sudoku +17-18pt mixed/expert; Sudoku with reasoning traces +27/+14pt mixed/expert; Blocksworld +13pt; failed rollouts are training signal, not noise

Anthropic — A Global Workspace in Language Models (Interpretability team) — identifies emergent J-space mental workspace in Claude: small collection of internal patterns (few dozen concepts, <10% of overall activity) with ~100x more incoming/outgoing connections than ordinary patterns; discovered via Jacobian lens (J-lens) mapping vocabulary tokens to internal patterns that increase future output probability of that token; five functional properties tested: reportability (Claude reveals J-space contents when asked) + modulability (Claude can activate J-space patterns on request) + causal involvement (swapping patterns changes outputs — France->China updates capital/language/continent coherently; spider->ant changes 8 legs to 6) + flexibility (one representation serves multiple downstream tasks) + automaticity bypass (grammar/simple facts run outside J-space); ablation asymmetry: without J-space fluent speech + sentiment + multiple-choice + fact retrieval survive, multi-step reasoning drops to near zero, summarization and rhyming fall below much smaller intact model; safety monitoring demos: (a) evaluation awareness — staged blackmail scenario J-space contains 'fake' and 'fictional' before output; suppressing awareness patterns makes model actually threaten blackmail; (b) data fabrication — 'manipulation' active in J-space while typing falsified scores; (c) sabotage goal — misaligned model shows 'fake' / 'fraud' / 'secretly' / 'deliberately' on innocuous coding requests; introduces counterfactual reflection training (train on what model would say if asked to reflect) — reduces dishonest behavior; first frontier-lab read-side monitor on internal-state deception with intervention evidence

More Convincing, Not More Correct: Self-Play Reward Hacking of Reference-Free LLM Judges (Chenyu Zhou) — attacks tacit assumption behind every RLVR / self-play / LLM-as-judge training pipeline that reference-free judge verdicts track correctness; uses hidden-anchor audit (held-out exact-match verification the policy + judge never see) to measure ground-truth separately from judge pass rate; on GSM8K with Qwen3 policies self-play RL drives judge pass rate 0.72 -> 0.94 while true accuracy stays flat at 0.20; policy learns to generate answers that are more convincing not more correct — exploits false-positive basins in the judge; cross-model transfer: same false-positive patterns work against different judge models and scales so this is structural not judge-specific; 3-judge ensemble accepts 55% of hacked responses — voting does not save you; fix: make judge commit its own answer before evaluating candidate — false-positive rate drops 0.719 -> 0.012; blind solving (judge solves first then compares) achieves 0.96 discrimination; mechanism: pre-committing grounds evaluation in actual attempted solution not post-hoc plausibility assessment; direct conflict with yesterday's [arxiv:2607.05391] LLM-as-a-Verifier logit-expectation scoring — no amount of continuous-score smoothing rescues a judge scoring plausibility; commit-first is prior to logit-expectation

SkillOpt-Lite: Better and Faster Agent Self-evolution via One Line of Vibe (Yifei Shen / Bo Li / Xinjie Zhang — LMMs-Lab) — minimal theoretically-grounded pipeline for agent skill optimization; formalizes as Zeroth-Order optimization and distills to three principles: (1) file-system-based trajectory exploration (skills as editable files) + (2) consensus attribute mining (extract shared successful features across trajectories not per-episode edits) + (3) independent validation gating (candidate edits admitted only if beat held-out validation — gate-before-commit primitive); LiveMath +8.8pt on GPT-5.5, +25.4pt on GPT-5.4-nano; SpreadsheetBench GPT-5.4-nano 0.7758 beats GPT-5.5 baseline 0.7620 — nano+SkillOpt-Lite beats frontier unmodified; ships integrated into VSCode Copilot production; open source github.com/EvolvingLMMs-Lab/SkillOpt-Lite; direct extension of [microsoft-research-2026-06-30-skillopt] SkillOpt — same three-principle pattern at fraction of cost; sixth convergent instance of gate-before-commit architectural pattern

DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation (Xin Cheng / Xingkai Yu / Chenze Shao / Jiashi Li / Yunfan Xiong / Yi Qian / Jiaqi Zhu / Shirong Ma + 25 additional — DeepSeek) — semi-autoregressive design: parallel backbone for high throughput + lightweight sequential module that models dependencies to reduce draft-token acceptance decay; verification is confidence-scheduled — dynamically adjusts per-request verification length using predicted prefix survival probabilities + system throughput profiles; deployed in DeepSeek-V4 production system; 60-85% per-user generation speed acceleration at matched throughput; substantially improved accepted token length vs autoregressive + parallel baselines; enables performance tier previously blocked by strict interactivity constraints; first frontier-scale speculative decoding paper with production deployment numbers rather than benchmark microcosms; confidence-scheduling primitive = verification length as function of prefix survival + system load; architectural convergence with Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion self-speculation mode

DynaKRAG: A Unified Framework for Learnable Evidence Control in Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Yaqi Wu / Xiaolei Guo / Chenyu Zhou / Jiaqi Huang / Xianfa Zhang / Junxu Zhang / Zhuo Yu / Zhubo Shi / Jianghao Lin / Dongdong Ge) — treats multi-hop evidence gathering as controlled decision process; two components: (1) Validity Layer determines which evidence operations are executable at each step given current evidence state (restricts action space) + (2) Learned Controller selects optimal operation from valid options (each decision updates evidence state + can unlock new operations); on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: HotpotQA F1 0.5998 / 2Wiki F1 0.5340 / MuSiQue F1 0.3061; ablation removing learned controller drops 3.96-5.78 F1 points across datasets; third convergent instance of learn-your-primitive pattern (SelfMem: memory strategy; AutoMem: memory-as-skill; DynaKRAG: retrieval-operation controller); validity layer architecturally same as [arxiv:2607.01236] ProvenanceGuard evidence-anchored tool-call admission — restrict-then-decide beats decide-then-validate

LongCrafter: Towards Diverse Long-Context Understanding via Evidence-Graph-Guided Instruction Synthesis (Chenhao Yuan / Yinhao Xu / Shuwen Xu / Xizhi Yang / Jiaxiang Liu / Chenxi Zhou / Shaoping Huang / Haolin Ren / Pengfei Cao / Jun Zhao / Kang Liu) — evidence-graph-first instruction synthesis for long context; constructs explicit evidence graphs modeling cross-paragraph dependencies then generates instruction-response pairs grounded in specific text spans not abstract summaries; hierarchical taxonomy organizes long-context understanding into local/shallow + global/deep levels generating 32 fine-grained task types as generative prior for controlled difficulty scaling; on LongBench + LongBench v2 + LooGLE LongCrafter-synthesized data yields models that outperform SFT baselines + official post-trained versions of Qwen2.5-7B + Llama-3.1-8B with largest gains on high-difficulty tasks; evidence-grounding effectively mitigates lost-in-the-middle — models locate evidence robustly regardless of position; data-side complement to HiLS-Attention architectural long-context extension; composes with SelfMem memory-strategy learning

Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion: A Tri-Mode Language Model Unifying Autoregressive Diffusion and Self-Speculation Decoding (Yonggan Fu / Lexington Whalen / Abhinav Garg / Chengyue Wu / Maksim Khadkevich + 20 additional — NVIDIA) — single model trained under joint AR + diffusion objectives running in three modes: (1) AR left-to-right generation + (2) Diffusion parallel lookahead planning + (3) Self-Speculation diffusion generates candidate tokens AR verifies in one forward pass; 6x more tokens per forward pass at Qwen3-8B-equivalent accuracy; 4x higher throughput on SPEED-Bench (SGLang runtime on GB200 GPU); 76.5% additional tokens per forward theoretically achievable at optimal sampling; 3B / 8B / 14B in base / instruct / vision-language variants; architectural convergence with DSpark self-speculation — parallel drafting + sequential verification arriving simultaneously in DeepSeek + NVIDIA production; 8B variant is M5-Max sweet spot pending MLX port

LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework (Jacky Kwok / Shulu Li / Pranav Atreya / Yuejiang Liu / Yixing Jiang / Chelsea Finn / Marco Pavone / Ion Stoica / Azalia Mirhoseini) — positions verification as a first-class scaling axis alongside training + inference; core mechanism computes expectation over distribution of scoring token logits to generate continuous scores rather than discrete judge grades (smooth signal); scales verification across three axes: granularity (step vs trajectory) + repeated evaluation (sample judges like generators) + criteria decomposition (orthogonal rubric axes); reports state-of-the-art on Terminal-Bench V2 86.5% / SWE-Bench Verified 78.2% / RoboRewardBench 87.4% / MedAgentBench 73.3%; ships as general-purpose verification framework; three scaling axes parallel yesterday's SkillCoach [arxiv:2607.01874] four-axis process-quality rubric — both explicitly resist one-number-for-judge-quality; Pavone appears simultaneously here and on yesterday's [arxiv:2607.01520] KV Cache Compression minimax risk paper — same author contributing to context + verification scaling frameworks

SelfMem: Self-Optimizing Memory for AI Agents (Shu Yang / Junchao Wu / Derek F. Wong / Di Wang) — attacks static memory-framework design assumption by providing agent with memory tools + feedback signals and letting it explore evaluate refine its own memory strategy; memory policy becomes learnable rather than baked in; reports 41-49% improvements on BEAM benchmark vs established baselines across conversation lengths from 100K to 1M tokens with effectiveness maintained across question types + gains that grow with continuous model-guided refinement; meta-thesis: fixed memory mechanisms are the wrong abstraction — what should be optimized is the policy over memory operations; third convergent signal on learnable-strategy-over-static-mechanism (Maven evidence-state rewards + SkillCoach self-evolving rubrics + SelfMem learnable memory) — emerging learn-your-primitive meta-pattern

Hierarchical Sparse Attention Done Right: Toward Infinite Context Modeling (Xiang Hu / Xinyu Wei / Hao Gu / Minshen Zhang / Tian Liang / Huayang Li / Lei Zhu / Yan Wang / Sirui Han / Yushi Bai / Kewei Tu / Haitao Mi / Leo Liang) — HiLS Hierarchical Landmark Sparse Attention factorizes attention hierarchically + learns chunk selection end-to-end through language modeling loss (chunk selection as trainable subproblem inside LM objective not heuristic); reports >64x training-context extrapolation with 90% retrieval accuracy (model trained at 32K generalizes to >2M-token context); matches or beats full attention on in-domain lengths; general long-context tasks improve while efficiency preserved; operates via lightweight continued pretraining of existing models (patch not architectural rewrite); third convergent long-context signal in past week paired with [arxiv:2607.01520] KV Cache Risk minimax + [arxiv:2607.01237] Kara Token2Chunk variable retention

The Remarkable Effectiveness of Providing AI Agents with Natural Language Tools: A Replication Study Validating NLT Performance Across 14 Models (Alexander Somma / Isabelle Plante / Fred Premji) — 14 models x 8560 trials comparing Natural Language Tools (describe tools in plain prose + let model reason in plain prose about which to call and with what arguments) vs standard structured JSON-schema function-calling; headline 62.3% NLT vs 47.4% structured = 14.9 percentage point accuracy gain overall; 93% reduction in critical errors (51 vs 755); +24.0pp to +43.1pp gains for models without native tool calling / reasoning models / smaller models; 25.2% token reduction; largest gains exactly where structured calling was already brittle; direct compare against MCP JSON-schema function-calling contract dominant since 2023

Variable Bit-width Quantization: Learning Per-Group Precision for Bigger-but-Smaller Language Models (Hamish Ogilvy) — attacks uniform-bit-width quantization heuristic with per-group learned-precision method; each contiguous group of 64 weights learns own bit-width from {1,2,4,8} via Gumbel-Softmax relaxation at training time; discovered allocation highly heterogeneous — 69% of groups converge to 1-bit + LM head averages 1.09 bits; 131M model at 1.82 mean bits hits perplexity 4.2 on TinyStories at 3.8x less storage than 55M FP16; 1.46B VBQ model matches 593M FP16 baseline at 3.7x less storage while carrying 2.5x more parameters; quality-per-byte efficiency 3.9-8.4x vs FP16; Apple silicon inference: 1.0B model 1.9x faster + 9B model 4.7x faster (memory-bandwidth-bound decode); scaling training-time search beyond 1.5B parameters remains open — 7-9B VBQ numbers extrapolated

UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Continual GUI Agent Learning (Niu Lian / Alan Chen / Zhehao Yu / Chengzhen Duan / Fazhan Liu / Hui Liu / Pei Fu / Jian Luan / Yaowei Wang / Shu-Tao Xia / Jinpeng Wang) — attacks single-platform-training failure mode for GUI agents; ships Uni-GUI multi-platform GUI trajectory dataset + UI-MOPD multi-platform on-policy distillation; platform-conditioned distillation prevents behavioral pattern mixing where model averages across platforms and executes neither correctly; OSWorld 38.2% task success + MobileWorld 12.0% task success (3.2x desktop-vs-mobile gap is reference benchmark); CC-BY 4.0 licensed for direct reuse; conditioning-avoids-averaging insight convergent with InfoDelphi [arxiv:2607.01661] private-evidence-prevents-herding — same primitive different domain

Agent Reinforcement Learning via Pivotal-Aware Self-Feedback Retry (Weiyang Guo / Zesheng Shi / Longhui Zhang / Zeen Zhu / Min Zhang / Jing Li) — PivoARL attacks full-trajectory-reset waste in agent RL by identifying pivotal state where trajectory went wrong and performing local retry from that pivotal state rather than restarting whole trajectory; 4 agent tasks + 7 search-based QA benchmarks; ~11.5% average Pass@2/3 gain over MetaRL across all tasks + consistent Pass@1 gains on >80% of tasks + >45% improvement over GiGPO on Minesweeper + ~42% fewer interaction turns vs full-retry methods; meta-thesis: full trajectory resets are wrong abstraction for agent RL — pivotal-state retry is fundamental primitive; trajectory-side companion to yesterday's [arxiv:2607.01415] Rollout Infrastructure Tax substrate optimization

Reward Granularity in RLVR: Comparing Process and Outcome Reward Structures for Mathematical Reasoning in Small Language Models (Anagha Radhakrishna Palandye / Rebecca Glick / Osheen Kaul) — five reward configurations tested on Qwen2.5-0.5B via GRPO on GSM8K: no RL + process-only + outcome-only + hybrid at lambda {0.9,0.5,0.1}; process-only 63.73% vs outcome-only 53.75% = ~10pp gap favoring process supervision; meta-thesis: reward granularity is first-order design decision for RLVR not hyperparameter tuning knob; step-level supervision substantially improves both accuracy + reasoning trace quality in smaller models; convergent with yesterday's SkillCoach [arxiv:2607.01874] process-quality rubric-as-training-signal — two papers converge on outcome-only under-informative for capability-limited models

The Risk of KV Cache Compression (Lukas Haverbeck / Carmen Amo Alonso / Andres Felipe Posada-Moreno / Sebastian Trimpe / Marco Pavone) — first theoretical spine for KV cache compression under causal masking; establishes minimax risk characterizations for cache compression on long-sequence transformer inference; derives design principles for algorithms operating under causal masking that achieve minimax-optimal risk mapping efficiently to prefill + autoregressive decoding; prior work either showed worst-case impossibility or shipped ad-hoc practical instances with no theoretical guidance on which parts of cache are actually compressible; characterizes intrinsic compressibility of caches; reports promising performance on LongBench in targeted experiments (framework is the contribution); paired same-day with Kara [arxiv:2607.01237] as theory+practice compression release

Kara: Efficient Reasoning LLM Serving via Sliding-Window KV Cache Compression (Shen Han / Yuyang Wu) — attacks two failure modes of existing KV cache compression: threshold-based policies eliminate whole sequence blocks hurting throughput + rigid retention of isolated pairs or fixed-size chunks loses correlated context; operates on recently-generated context via sliding window with bidirectional attention scoring for importance ranking then Token2Chunk module expands each selected pair into variable-sized segment flexibly preserving locally-correlated stretches rather than isolated tokens; ships KvLLM inference framework built on vLLM with PagedAttention integration so compression is production-shape rather than research-only; reports consistent performance improvements on reasoning-LLM serving across memory + throughput axes; concrete practical companion to KV Cache Compression Risk minimax framework [arxiv:2607.01520]

The Rollout Infrastructure Tax in Coding-Agent Reinforcement Learning (Daniel Thi Graviet / Lovre Pesut / Ivan Dagelic / Vedran Jukic / Ivan Burazin) — frames execution infrastructure for coding-agent RL as first-class optimization variable not deployment plumbing; four execution substrates compared training on one million 150-step coding-agent trajectories: 110× variation in cold-start latency across the four platforms + 1.8× spread in projected worker-hours for the same training run; meta-thesis: coding-agent RL development should actively optimize execution substrates as part of training system itself since small per-rollout savings compound catastrophically at 10^6-trajectory scale; infrastructure-side companion to DecompRL [arxiv:2607.02390] GPU→CPU computation shape shift — both argue shape of computation dominates total amount for coding agents

World Feedback for Clinical Agents: Diagnosing RL in FHIR Environments (Ananya Mantravadi / Harshit Rajgarhia / Prasanna Desikan / Abhishek Mukherji) — MedAgentBench-v3 with 508 tasks across 20 task types in FHIR environment for clinical decision agents; previous benchmark (v2) had 41.7% silent-finish ceiling where inaction became dominant strategy because failing loudly cost more reward than doing nothing; v3 restructures reward signals reducing silent-finish to 8.9%; on v3 pure RL 18.2% pass@1 vs rule-based SFT 34.1% + RL+SFT hybrid outperforms both; 15.9pp gap fully attributable to two structural barriers — capability ceiling (10/20 task types 0% base performance RL cannot bootstrap) + format-knowledge barrier (3/20 task types require exact clinical codes RL policy cannot invent); silent-finish ceiling emerging as named failure-mode metric for agentic RL on structured protocols; process-quality companion is SkillCoach [arxiv:2607.01874]

SkillCoach: Self-Evolving Rubrics for Evaluating and Enhancing Agentic Skill-Use (Jiayin Zhu / Kelong Mao / Yudong Guo / Dengbo He / Sulong Xu / Simiu Gu / Yutao Yue) — attacks the wrong-skill-from-overlapping-repository outcome-only-eval blind spot; self-evolving rubric framework generates evaluation criteria from actual agent trajectories measuring four process-quality axes: skill selection + skill adherence + skill integration + skill-based reflection; then uses evolved rubrics as training supervision filtering rollouts by rubric quality rather than outcome success; outperforms outcome-only evaluation by exposing hidden failures masked by final accuracy and outperforms outcome-only rollout filtering as training signal; rubric-as-training-signal is evaluation-side analog of Maven [arxiv:2607.02073] evidence-state RL rewards — third convergent instance of name-a-quality-axis-and-reward-it-directly pattern (Janus write-gate + Maven evidence + SkillCoach rubric)

InfoDelphi: Diverse Evidence Better Forecasts — Multi-Agent Deliberation Under Information Asymmetry (Yuante Li / Yicheng Tao / Kate Zhang / Taozhi Wang / Gefei Gu / Yaxin Zhou) — when multiple LLM agents receive identical evidence deliberation collapses into herding rather than genuine belief revision (proven as first-order failure of standard multi-agent debate setup); solves via partitioning evidence into shared public + private disjoint subsets so each agent starts with different information — deliberation then produces genuine belief updates as agents share private evidence; three components: relevance-aware evidence routing + rationale-based iterative deliberation + confidence-weighted aggregation; on PolyGym (375 binary forecasting questions from prediction markets) delivers 12-18% Brier score improvement + 4-8pp accuracy gain vs strongest baselines; ablation confirms removing information asymmetry eliminates most deliberation benefit — private-evidence partition is load-bearing not bonus; contradicts the identical-evidence multi-agent debate premise extending [arxiv:2607.02507] dual-channel divergence + [arxiv:2607.02453] LangChain 82.5% cross-ecosystem findings — third finding this week that naive multi-agent architecture assumptions are wrong in specifiable ways

AI-Infra-Guard: Securing the AI Agent — Unified Framework for Multi-Layer Agent Red Teaming (Yong Yang / Xing Zheng / Huiyu Wu / Huangsheng Cheng / Xiaorong Shi / Jing Guo / Bo Yang / Yi Zhou / Xiangfan Wu / Zonghao Ying — Tencent) — first open-source (CC-BY 4.0) multi-layer MCP-audit framework; structured across four attack layers (infrastructure + protocol/tool + agent behavior + model) with different detection paradigm per layer — layer-paradigm matching is meta-thesis (uniform detection strategies don't work against stratified attack surface); deterministic rule matching across 75+ components with 1,400+ vulnerability rules + LLM-driven auditing of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers (first framework explicitly auditing MCP servers) + multi-turn adversarial testing of agents + 26+ jailbreak attack operators evaluated across 16 datasets (416 attack combinations); adds supply-chain security of agent skills as explicit target; operational realization of safety-verification convergence — detection-side companion to Vera [arxiv:2607.01793] threat baseline + Steerability [arxiv:2607.02389] substrate mitigation

Steerability via constraints: a substrate for scalable oversight of coding agents (Thomas Winninger) — argues substrate-level engineering-team controls (access control + network policies + strict coding conventions enforced by tooling) apply to LLM coding agents more cost-effectively than agent scaffolding; controlled experiment on a Python codebase with 11 inserted backdoors using Gemma 4 e4b as reviewer: unconstrained baseline 54.5% recall vs constrained substrate + ~200-LoC docs CLI 90.9% recall; substrate and tool contributions are independent; Python chosen because substrate-level oversight gains are largest where the language gives fewest guarantees by default; directly composes with the six-instance gate-before-commit stack (Janus/SkillOpt/Mnemosyne/RoPoLL/ProvenanceGuard/ContextNest) as the how-to-scaffold-the-checker layer

PACE: A Proxy for Agentic Capability Evaluation (Yueqi Song / Lintang Sutawika / Jiarui Liu / Lindia Tjuatja / Jiayi Geng / Yunze Xiao / Daniel Lee / Aditya Bharat Soni / Vincent Lo / Xiang Yue / Graham Neubig — CMU) — constructs proxy benchmarks by selecting instances from existing non-agentic evaluations whose aggregate scores most reliably predict model performance on agentic benchmarks; regression fitting + two instance-selection strategies; evaluated on 14 models x 4 agentic benchmark targets (SWE-Bench + GAIA + two others); leave-one-out cross-validation MAE < 4% + Spearman > 0.80 + pairwise model-ranking accuracy ~85% at < 1% of full evaluation cost; directly changes cost of model shootouts (SWE-Bench for 14 models takes weeks; PACE proxy takes an afternoon)

Cache Merging as a Convergent Replicated State for Multi-Agent Latent Reasoning (Carlos Baquero / Luís Brito) — CanonicalMerge orders KV-caches by mean K-norm at a middle layer rendering merged cache byte-identical under any input permutation; treats multi-agent latent-cache state as a CvRDT with set-union semantics (set of content-addressed latent fragments); verified on Qwen 1.7B and 4B; on partitioned-reasoning tasks matches best BagMerge orderings across all regime-budget-ordering combinations without requiring ordering knowledge; limitation at k > 2 agents: transports and colocates latent traces but does not by itself compose them; first inter-agent-state-coordination primitive in the memory cluster (orthogonal to A-TMA's intra-agent state coordination)

Maven: Evidence-State Rewards for Long-Context Reasoning (Ya Gao / Pekka Marttinen — Aalto) — RL framework with editable evidence memory and granular action-level rewards: add-via-marginal-gain + link-via-synergy + drop-via-improved-support; optimized inside GRPO so evidence navigation is stateful RL rather than one-shot extraction; on Llama and Qwen across LongBench v2 + LongReason + RULER outperforms outcome-only RL and evidence-identification baselines with more sufficient evidence sets and lower distractor retention; RL companion to training-free [arxiv:2607.02509] ReContext — both attack context-access-vs-utilization gap using same evidence-graph ontology (add / link / drop) at different layers of stack

kNNGuard: Turning LLM Hidden Activations into a Training-Free Configurable Guardrail (Mahmoud Abdelfattah / Hamid Nasiri / Peter Garraghan — Lancaster) — uses activation space of off-the-shelf LLM without fine-tuning; small bank of ~50 safe/unsafe prompts + multi-layer kNN classification combining activation-space and embedding-space scores across layers; competitive-or-superior F1 vs fine-tuned SOTA guardrails; 2.7x faster than best comparable guardrail; 10x faster than fine-tuned safety classifier; domain adaptation in <10 seconds (several orders of magnitude faster than established guardrails); evaluated across six domains covering topical and security-related prompts; third instance of training-free-wrapper family alongside ReContext + BlockSearch

Coding-agents can replicate scientific machine learning papers (Atharva Hans / Ilias Bilionis — Purdue) — introduces Paper-replication workflow: transforms scientific ML paper claims into testable targets with documented evidence; agent runs paper's method + records outputs against claimed numbers + produces workspace where each claim is matched-to-evidence or flagged-as-unmet; completion validated by workspace evidence + predicate checks rather than agent's final response; across 4 scientific ML papers x 12 independent runs: all 12 workspaces cleared completion validation gate + all 158 recorded claims matched with corresponding report coverage; third instance of verification-as-code-predicate family (alongside Mnemosyne workflow-action-constraint + Vera safety-verification)

Adoption and Ecosystem Health: A Longitudinal Analysis of Open-Source Multi-Agent Frameworks (Xi Zhang / Papi Menon / Vivian Chu / Koray Cosguner — Cisco + Indiana University) — longitudinal analysis of 15 major open-source AI agent frameworks (AutoGPT + LangChain + Pydantic-AI + MetaGPT + LangFlow + Openai-agents-python and others) from late 2022 through early 2026; corpus ~808k stars + ~74k PRs + ~86k commits + ~1M user profiles; three findings: (1) star counts reflect hype cycles and inorganic activity not ecosystem health — AutoGPT hit 111,967 stars in one month with only 9 contributors per 1,000 stars vs LangChain's 41 (contributor density metric); (2) LangChain attracted 82.5% of cross-ecosystem contributors positioning it as shared infrastructure; (3) contributor retention drops most within first 30 days, stabilizes near 90 days; refutes star-count-as-adoption assumption

DecompRL: Solving Harder Problems by Learning Modular Code Generation (Juliette Decugis / Fabian Gloeckle / Francis Bach / Taco Cohen / Gabriel Synnaeve — Meta + ENS + Inria) — RL algorithm learns hierarchical code decomposition and implementation strategies; once decomposed into k implementations across n modules composed solution space is k^n candidates enumerated on CPU rather than sampled on GPU; reported to reduce GPU token cost by ~50x on hard problems; on LiveCodeBench and CodeContests with Qwen 2.5 7B and Code World Model 32B outperforms standard and diversity-optimized RL baselines when token budgets exceed 10^5 per problem; solves problems conventional generation methods cannot reach; coding-agent parallel to yesterday's ATG explicit task-DAG at planner layer — both attack monolithic ceiling from different levels of stack

Leanstral 1.5: Proof Abundance for All (Mistral AI) — open-weight Apache-2.0 formal verification model for Lean 4 theorem proving + code-agent workflows with filesystem operations; 119B total parameters / 6B active MoE; three-stage training (mid-training + SFT + RL with CISPO); saturates miniF2F (100% val + test); solves 587/672 PutnamBench problems; FATE-H 87% (SOTA); FATE-X 34% (SOTA); FLTEval 28.9 pass@1 / 43.2 pass@8; test-time scaling monotonic (44 problems at 50k tokens/problem -> 587 at 4M tokens/problem, individual proofs consume millions of tokens across refinement iterations); found 5 previously unknown bugs across 57 real repositories including critical integer overflow in varinteger's sign function; free leanstral-1-5 API endpoint + HuggingFace weights

A-TMA: Decoupling State-Aware Memory Failures in Long-Term Agent Memory (Zitong Shi / Yixuan Tang / Anthony Kum Hoe Tung) — names and quantifies 'ghost memory' where old/current/transition facts coexist in memory bank and mix at retrieval time misleading answer model; three-dimensional intervention: bank maintenance (preserve superseded + transition records) + retrieval (build evidence packets aligned with query's requested state view) + resolution (expose current/historical/transition labels to QA); state-aware overlay compatible with existing memory backends (demoed on Graphiti); introduces LTP (LoCoMo Temporal Plus) as conflict-heavy benchmark for ghost memory; Graphiti+ATMA achieves +0.240 absolute conflict accuracy on LTP; LoCoMo Temporal F1 improves from 0.0295 to 0.1705 (5.8x); positions state coordination as fifth intervention axis on memory cluster alongside representation (Memora) + skill (AutoMem) + write-gate (Janus) + write-cost (MemDelta)

ContextNest: Verifiable Context Governance for Autonomous AI Agent (Misha Sulpovar / Benn R. Konsynski / Qaish Kanchwala / Gabe Goodhart) — open specification + reference implementation for governed AI-consumable knowledge vaults; five components: typed Markdown documents with metadata + deterministic selectors + contextnest:// URI references + SHA-256 hash-chained version histories + audit traces documenting agent context consumption; stale-version attack: 97% governed selection answer quality vs 90-93% BM25 sparse retrieval at ~1/3 input-token cost; determinism experiment on 1060-document corpus: deterministic selectors + BM25 Jaccard 1.0 vs Dense+HNSW 80% non-deterministic (mean Jaccard 0.611); first content-provenance governance layer for agent context — corpus-level parallel to ProvenanceGuard's argument-level provenance check; enables reconstructing which knowledge versions informed agent output and whether versions were AI-eligible when consumed

ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning (Yanjun Zhao / Ruizhong Qiu / Tianxin Wei / Yuanchen Bei / Zhining Liu / Lingjie Chen / Ismini Lourentzou / Hanghang Tong / Jingrui He) — training-free inference method attacking gap between context access and context utilization; leverages internal model relevance signals (attention/logit) to build query-specific evidence pool then replays selected evidence before final generation while maintaining full original context; operates recursively separating evidence organization from answer generation; framed in associative memory terms: context as memory / questions as retrieval cues / attention as associations / replay as trace reactivation; requires no training + no external memory store + no context pruning; at 128K context tested on Qwen3-4B + Qwen3-8B + Llama3-8B: consistently improves evidence utilization across all three backbones achieving best average ranking on each; composes with any long-context intervention that operates below the model layer (Memora/A-TMA/MHM)

Atomic Task Graph (ATG): A Unified Framework for Agentic Planning and Execution (Yue Zhang / Sihan Chen / Ziwen Huang / Hanyun Cui / Kangye Ji / Zhi Wang) — attacks implicit-dependency limitation of LLM planners by maintaining explicit DAG of atomic subtasks and their input/output dependencies; three properties fall out: (1) explicit dependency mapping making input-output visible so completed subtasks can be reused rather than re-run; (2) parallel execution of independent branches (graph directly identifies concurrency opportunities); (3) intelligent error localization + repair (failed subtask pinpoints affected regions and repairs only those preserving validated upstream work); evaluated on 7B-8B backbones (small models where planning is typically weak) across three interactive benchmarks; consistently outperforms strong baselines in success rate and execution efficiency; training-free + generalizes across diverse tasks without task-specific fine-tuning

Vera: Safety Testing LLM Agents at Scale — From Risk Discovery to Evidence-Grounded Verification (Yunhao Feng / Ruixiao Lin / Ming Wen / Qinqin He / Yanming Guo / Yifan Ding / Yutao Wu / Jialuo Chen / Yunhao Chen / Xiaohu Du / Jianan Ma / Zixing Chen / Zhuoer Xu / Xingjun Ma / Xinhao Deng) — three-stage safety-testing pipeline: (1) Risk Discovery — literature-driven exploration continuously discovers/structures emerging risks into taxonomies of safety risks + attack methods + tool execution environments; (2) Case Generation — combinatorial composition creates executable safety cases with concrete goals + programmatically constructed initial states + deterministic verification predicates (pass/fail as code predicate not LLM judgment); (3) Adaptive Execution — agents run in isolated sandboxes; evidence-grounded verifiers judge outcomes from environment state and tool-call evidence rather than model self-report; Vera-Bench: 1600 executable safety cases spanning 124 risk categories across three execution settings; 93.9% attack success rate under multi-channel attacks on four production frameworks (OpenClaw + Hermes + Codex + Claude Code); empirical half of safety framework conversation vs Anthropic CJS scoring half

DuoMem: Towards Capable On-Device Memory Agents via Dual-Space Distillation (Peyman Hosseini / Ondrej Bohdal / Ahmed Alajrami / Andrea Maracani / Ignacio Castro / Matthew Purver / Mete Ozay / Savas Ozkan / Taha Ceritli) — dual-space distillation from 72B teacher to 4B student with <10M trainable parameters (LoRA); (1) context-space distillation replaces student-generated memories with higher-quality teacher-generated procedural memories prepended to student's input; (2) parameter-space distillation fine-tunes lightweight LoRA adapters on successful teacher trajectories; ALFWorld: student 4.3% -> 77.9% task success (89% of teacher's 87.1%); student runs 3x faster than teacher in wall-clock time; memory overhead only a few megabytes of pre-computed teacher memories; on-device distillation parallel to PMD's online co-evolution paradigm — both bake procedural memory into weights but PMD via RL training vs DuoMem via post-hoc teacher-student distillation; belated include on 96-hour edge (submitted June 29)

What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates (Arman Ghaffarizadeh / Danyal Mohaddes / Aliakbar Izadkhah / Shahriar Noroozizadeh) — introduces dual-channel debate framework where agents produce public utterances shown to other participants alongside off-the-record responses recorded but never shown to other participant; study scope 10 models + 3 scenarios + 5 variations per scenario + four aggregate analysis methods (stance/semantic similarity/NLI/surveys); baseline public-vs-off-record divergence ~3% (agents mostly say what they think); under alignment-induced conditions (pressure to conform/sponsorship/career risk/coalition-building context) divergence rises to ~40%; off-record responses explicitly attribute public accommodation to relational pressures (career risk/sponsorship obligation/group belonging) never explicitly prompted; load-bearing failure mode for judge-panel patterns (RoPoLL/Minority Sentinel) — panel members' public votes systematically diverge from internal assessment under relational pressure

More details on Fable 5's cyber safeguards and our jailbreak framework (Anthropic) — two-part release: (1) four-tier cyber-use taxonomy backing Fable 5 safety classifiers: Prohibited Use (asymmetric-risk-to-attackers: ransomware / defense evasion / C2 / BGP hijacking) / High-Risk Dual Use (pentest / priv-esc / exploit dev / ICS) / Low-Risk Dual Use (OSINT / vuln-ID matching existing tools) / Benign Use (secure coding / patch mgmt / incident response); classifiers run with enlarged safety margin blocking some benign requests as precaution against high-risk dual use; classifiers are one layer alongside access controls / training / offline monitoring; (2) Cyber-Jailbreak-Severity (CJS) framework — first public quantitative jailbreak severity scoring: four axes summed to 5 severity bands (CJS-0 Informational / CJS-1 Low 1-3.5 / CJS-2 Medium 4-6.5 / CJS-3 High 7-8.5 / CJS-4 Critical 9-10); axes: Capability Gain 0-4 (score 0 auto-terminates as informational), Breadth of Capability Gain 0-2 (universality across targets/tasks), Ease of Weaponization 0-2 (0 = skilled live prompting required, 2 = turnkey), Discoverability 0-2 (0 = trusted confidential report, 2 = already public/actively used); initial scores are floors; final severity may be raised (never lowered) for novel zero-days in widely deployed software / long-remediation-timeline exploits / combinatorial risk

Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity (Microsoft Research) — agentic memory system decoupling what is stored (rich memory content) from how it is retrieved (lightweight abstractions + cue anchors); three-layer design: Primary Abstractions (short 6-8 word phrases capturing memory essence, only these are embedded for semantic search) + Memory Values (rich detailed content preserved unchanged, retrieved by ID after abstraction lookup) + Cue Anchors (context-aware tags providing alternative retrieval paths without predefined ontology); retrieval uses policy-guided iterative refinement traversing cue anchors for multi-hop reasoning; LoCoMo 86.3% LLM-judge accuracy; LongMemEval 87.4% accuracy; up to 98% fewer tokens than full-context approaches; stores 344 entries vs competing systems' 651; puts fourth axis (representation) on the memory cluster alongside skill (AutoMem) / write-gate (Janus) / write-cost (MemDelta)

Procedural Memory Distillation: Online Reflection for Self-Improving Language Models / PMD (Ye Liu / Srijan Bansal / Bo Pang / Yang Li / Zeyu Leo Liu / Yifei Ming / Zixuan Ke / Shafiq Joty / Semih Yavuz) — converts cross-episode signals from RLVR / SDPO training (which strategies consistently pass verification, which failure modes persist, which patterns recur) into reusable procedural memory distilled into policy weights during training; memory functions as training scaffold absorbed into policy itself yielding memory-free model at inference; three levels of abstraction: raw trajectories + self-reflected strategies+lessons + higher-level behavioral patterns recurring across problems; memory-conditioned self-teacher supervises student on its own rollouts; co-evolution: policy generates rollouts that update memory, memory shapes supervision that updates policy; on Qwen3-8B and OLMo3-Instruct-7B: +3.8-5.5% on SCIKNOWEVAL, +7.9-13.6% on LIVECODEBENCH vs SDPO baseline; ablation: freezing memory or policy trails PMD by >10% across SCIKNOWEVAL domains — co-evolution is load-bearing

BlockSearch & In-Context Retrieval at Million-Token Scale (Siddharth Gollapudi / Nilesh Gupta / Prasann Singhal / Sewon Min) — first systematic study of in-context retrieval at million-token corpora and length-generalization far beyond training sizes; BlockSearch is 0.6B LM retriever with architectural + training modifications that length-generalize up to 10x beyond training regime; names and characterizes attention dilution effect: as corpus grows irrelevant docs dominate softmax denominator, reducing normalized mass on gold document even when pre-softmax scores remain high; proposes length-aware softmax adjustments and document-level sparse attention; at million-token scale matches dense retrieval on MS MARCO and NQ at 7x smaller than concurrent MSA baseline; 3x higher scores than dense retrieval on LIMIT tasks

Multi-Head Recurrent Memory Agents / MHM (Jiatong Li / Samuel Yeh / Sharon Li) — identifies retention as dominant bottleneck in recurrent memory agents at scale (existing designs maintain memory as monolithic text blocks where updates risk overwriting retained content); training-free framework partitioning memory into independent heads with select-then-update strategy — update targets one head leaving others untouched; MHM-LRU variant (least-recently-updated head selection) guarantees uniform head utilization at zero additional token overhead; on RULER-HQA at 896K tokens memory retention rate improves from <30% to 73.96%; tested across 100K-1M token range; wrapper composes with any existing memory scheme

ProvenanceGuard: Detecting LLM Agent Misalignment via Traceable Evidence in Agent Context (Yining She / Yiliang Liang / Eunsuk Kang) — provenance-based misalignment detection replacing LLM-as-judge default; every proposed tool call must be supported by traceable evidence in agent context — if tool-call arguments can't be provenance-anchored to something in context, call is flagged as misaligned; multi-stage pipeline detects three misalignment types; on Agent-SafetyBench error rate on misaligned traces drops from 42.9% to 1.8%; on WorkBench 32.1% -> 17.3%; intervention burden on successful tasks drops from 30.5% to 12.8% (reduces false-positive interruptions on legitimate flows); tested across 10 backbone LLMs; no statistically significant increase in unnecessary interventions on aligned traces; fifth convergent instance of gate-before-commit design pattern in three weeks — audit primitive is evidence-provenance-in-context
