PACE: A Proxy for Agentic Capability Evaluation (Yueqi Song / Lintang Sutawika / Jiarui Liu / Lindia Tjuatja / Jiayi Geng / Yunze Xiao / Daniel Lee / Aditya Bharat Soni / Vincent Lo / Xiang Yue / Graham Neubig) — constructs proxy benchmarks from existing non-agentic evaluations to predict performance on costly agent benchmarks (SWE-Bench / GAIA / etc); two complementary selection strategies: target-relevance local selection (align with target benchmark distribution) + globally informative global selection (discriminate models across broad capability space); leave-one-out cross-validation MAE <4%, Spearman correlation >0.80, pairwise model-ranking accuracy ~85% at <1% of full agentic evaluation cost; evaluated across 4 target agentic benchmarks (including SWE-Bench and GAIA), 19 source non-agentic benchmarks, 14 models

PartRep: Learning What to Repeat for Decoder-Only LLMs (Andikawati P Widjaja / Yongjun Kim / Hyounghun Kim / Jaeho Lee) — prompt repetition (appending second copy of prompt before generation) redistributes grounding across positions in decoder-only causal-attention and improves reasoning but doubles KV cache + prefill cost; PartRep replaces full repetition with selective repetition of high-value tokens identified by token-wise negative log-likelihood (unpredictable tokens benefit most from late-position repetition); lightweight gate predicts high-NLL tokens from early-layer representations enabling mid-prefill selection via early exit; across 8 benchmarks (MMLU / GSM8K / RULER) and 3 model families (Qwen2.5 / Llama3.2 / Gemma4) retains most benefits of full repetition at 59.4% of KV cache and 79.0% of prefill FLOPs vs full repetition

AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill (Shengguang Wu / Hao Zhu / Yuhui Zhang / Xiaohan Wang / Serena Yeung-Levy — Stanford) — frames memory management as metamemory: two-loop optimization where strong LLM iteratively refines memory schemas / prompts / action vocabulary from agent trajectories (outer loop), then high-quality memory decisions from successful episodes train the target model to internalize memory proficiency (inner loop); treats file-system operations (create/read/update/delete on typed memory objects) as first-class trainable actions alongside task actions; on Crafter / MiniHack / NetHack (three procedurally generated long-horizon tasks) achieves ~2x-4x base agent performance improvement from memory optimization alone; 32B open-weight model reaches competitive performance with Claude Opus 4.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro Thinking; positions memory management as independently learnable high-leverage skill for long-horizon tasks

SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters (Yifan Yang / Xuemei Gao / Qi Dai / Bei Liu / Kai Qiu / Dongdong Chen / Chong Luo — Microsoft Research) — treats Claude-Code-style natural-language agent skill files as trainable parameters outside the frozen base model; structured optimization loop: forward pass runs task with current skill, backward pass has optimizer LLM propose bounded text edits (add/delete/replace), validation gating only accepts candidates that beat held-out validation, rejected-edit buffer informs future updates, epoch-wise slow updates consolidate; on six benchmarks × seven models × three execution modes (52 evaluation cells): GPT-5.5 direct chat 58.8% -> 82.3% (+23.5pp), SpreadsheetBench 41.8% -> 80.7%, OfficeQA 33.1% -> 72.1%; Qwen3.5-4B with trained skill outperforms larger baselines without fine-tuning; skills transfer across model scales and execution harnesses; open source at github.com/microsoft/SkillOpt

Self-GC: Self-Governing Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents (Xubin Hao / Hongjin Meng / Xin Yin / Jiawei Zhu / Chenpeng Cao) — reframes context management as runtime lifecycle control over indexed recoverable objects rather than post-hoc text cleanup; turns user interactions / tool operations / skill states into indexed objects, planner recommends compression actions, recoverable sidecars with cache-aware commits preserve rollback + prompt-cache economics; on 33-session test set 43.95% prefix token pruning while preserving 84.85% of future continuations (vs baselines 54.55%-69.70% pruning at unstated preservation); production 332 sessions no-impact rates 91.27%-94.58% (baselines 77.71%-87.46%); real-world daytime input-token reduction 10-15%, peak approaching 20%

MemSyco-Bench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Agent Memory (Zhishang Xiang / Zerui Chen / Yunbo Tang / Zhimin Wei / Ruqin Ning / Yujie Lin / Qinggang Zhang / Jinsong Su) — first benchmark separating retrieval quality from downstream decision quality in presence of memory; names memory-induced sycophancy as failure mode where faithful memory causes agent to over-align with user at cost of factual accuracy; five tasks: (1) reject memory as factual evidence when it shouldn't be, (2) respect memory's applicable scope, (3) resolve conflicts between memory and objective evidence, (4) track memory updates, (5) use valid memory for personalization; public GitHub

Mnemosyne: Agentic Transaction Processing for Validating and Repairing AI-generated Workflows (Edward Y. Chang / Longling Geng / Emily J. Chang) — runtime for validating and repairing AI-generated agent actions before they commit; framing: agent actions may be syntactically correct but outdated / impossible / contradictory / destructive, so 'anything may propose but only the runtime admits and commits'; append-only transition log + effective-state projection + dependency-safe compensation + active commitment records; proves 4 safety properties; rejects targeted violations across 9 falsification tests while accepting valid operations; <6% overhead for projection+validation; localized repair edits ~10x fewer operations than global recomputation; open source

Self-Evolving Agents with Anytime-Valid Certificates / SEA (Biswa Sengupta) — restricts self-modification to small steering adapter + versioned harness around frozen base model, uses anytime-valid gates to audit changes against error budget; certificates constrain modifications to those the frozen model can already produce; five verification mechanisms: best-of-N selection / micro-step search / self-authored reproduction oracles / search-layer control / self-repair — all without external grading, extracting signal from issue text alone; on SWE-Bench Verified subset (52 instances x 4 models) GLM 24 -> 28 (+4), GPT 29 -> 34 (+5, '65% best'); base-model capability dominates gain; event logs confirm mechanisms fired without regressions

What Survives Into Context: A Diagnostic for Budget-Constrained Multi-Hop RAG (Ananto Nayan Bala) — attacks document-recall-as-RAG-metric under budget constraints; introduces 'answer-in-context' (does gold answer survive as contiguous span in packed context) as counter-metric that predicts answer F1 substantially better than recall (r=0.39-0.55 vs 0.31); documents 4.6x performance gap on HotpotQA even when all relevant evidence was retrieved — evidence retrieved, answer didn't survive packing; proposes submodular maximization packing algorithm jointly optimizing relevance/query-coverage/representativeness/diversity — +5.1 F1 on HotpotQA at 160-token budgets vs heuristic baselines; caveat: gains conditional on multi-hop structure + moderate budgets + weak readers

A Task-State Representation for Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agents / TSR (Yujie Zheng / Zikang Liu / Xin Zhao / Ji-Rong Wen — Renmin University of China) — training-free wrapper around any base agent maintaining three structured elements: global instruction summary + dynamic subgoal progress tracker + transition-aware action verifier that continuously updates from before/after visual comparisons; addresses conflation of persistent task requirements with ephemeral screen states in long-horizon mobile GUI agents; up to +12 absolute point success-rate improvement on cross-application and memory-intensive tasks across four mobile-GUI benchmarks

Introducing Claude Sonnet 5 (Anthropic) — new Sonnet-tier release positioned as close to Opus 4.8 performance at lower pricing; API model ID claude-sonnet-5; pricing $2/M input + $10/M output introductory through Aug 31 2026, standard $3/$15; available Free/Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise/Claude Code/Claude Platform/API; updated tokenizer requires 1.0–1.35x more tokens vs Sonnet 4.6 for equivalent content (offsets sticker-price cut); cybersecurity capability substantially poorer than Opus 4.8 by design (0.0% on Firefox exploit development, framed as safety tradeoff); comparison references BrowseComp / OSWorld-Verified (Sonnet 4.6 updated to 78.5% under methodology adjustment) / Humanity's Last Exam (Sonnet 4.6 updated to 34.6% no-tools / 46.8% with-tools); Sonnet 5 headline numbers not published inline in launch post

Redeploying Fable 5 (Anthropic) — U.S. export controls on Fable 5 and Mythos 5 lifted; global availability resumes July 1 across Claude Platform / Claude.ai / Claude Code / Claude Cowork; original June 12 suspension triggered by Amazon research report demonstrating safeguard bypass extracting vulnerability-ID code; post-hoc analysis found every peer model tested (Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Kimi K2.7, Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, multiple Opus versions) could produce the same demonstration — Amazon bypass did not expose unique Mythos-level cyber capabilities; new safety classifier blocks specific reported bypass in >99% of cases via defense-in-depth (larger safety margin, blocks some benign requests to prevent jailbreaks); cloud re-enablement on AWS / Google Cloud / Microsoft Foundry underway; Pro/Max/Team/Select Enterprise included through July 7 (up to 50% of weekly usage), then usage-credit-billed

The Past Is Prologue: A Plug-in Controller for Selective Updates in Sequentially Evolving LLM Memory / Janus (Zihan Chen / Songwei Dong / Chengshuai Shi / Peng Wang / Song Wang / Cong Shen / Jundong Li) — frames memory-update problem: updates that help current task may overwrite useful knowledge, introduce over-specific rules, or bias final memory toward recent examples; Janus is method-agnostic plug-in controller sitting on top of any existing memory-update system deciding whether to accept each proposed write; Memory Momentum Trigger watches for suspicious deviations + hybrid test set evaluates proposed changes using representative task samples not full historical replay; +2.7 to +4.6pp accuracy over base updaters across six datasets, two backbone LLMs, two different memory updaters

Dockerless: Environment-Free Program Verifier for Coding Agents (Wenhao Zeng / Yuling Shi / Xiaodong Gu / Chao Hu / Chaofan Wang / Yuhao Cui / Hongting Zhou / Mengnan Qi / Jianqiao Wangni / Zhaojian Yu / Shuzheng Gao / Kai Cai / Shilin He — ByteDance) — verifier for coding-agent patches judging correctness via evidence gathered through agentic repository exploration, no execution environment; SWE-bench Verified 62.0% resolve rate, SWE-bench Multilingual 50.0%, SWE-bench Pro 35.2%; outperforms leading open-source verifier by 14.3 AUC points; surpasses Qwen3.5-9B baseline by 2.4/8.7/2.9 points across three benchmarks; matches environment-based post-training performance; enables coding-agent training pipelines that don't require Docker or per-repo environment setup

RoPoLL: Robust Panel of LLM Judges (Anish Acharya / Kris W Pan / Brian Verkhovsky) — proves conventional PoLL (mean/majority aggregation of LLM judges) incurs unbounded bias under any positive contamination when individual judges exhibit mode collapse / safety refusal / drift; RoPoLL replaces aggregation with geometric median (robust mean estimator, optimal breakdown point 1/2, no tuning knobs); 3-judge RoPoLL committee at 38B parameters beats Mistral-Large-3 (675B) by 1.31x on HelpSteer-2 under 30% bimodal-random corruption; dominates PoLL by ~19% on cross-dimensional attacks; tested across 13 open-weight judges (4B-675B) and four corruption regimes up to 50%; 18x parameter advantage at better accuracy

OpenLife: Toward Open-World Artificial Life with Autonomous LLM Agents (Atsushi Masumori / Itsuki Doi / Norihiro Maruyama / Ryosuke Takata / Takashi Ikegami — ALIFE 2026) — six LLM-driven agents run on open internet for ~12 weeks with budget-based metabolism (persistent operation gated on maintaining resources); architecture is society of asynchronous processes — memory / perception / evaluation — not one smart agent; agents equipped with persistent memory, tool access, financial capabilities; open-vocabulary LLM judgment replaces scalar reward; reports behavioral shifts, agent individuation, emergent social dynamics, and first self-earned external income; authors do not claim artificial life realized but that open-world ALIFE is viable experimental paradigm

ScarfBench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Enterprise Java Framework Migration (IBM Research) — open benchmark for cross-framework migration in Enterprise Java (Spring / Jakarta EE / Quarkus) measuring whether migrated applications actually build, deploy, preserve original behavior; 34 applications, 102 framework implementations, 204 migration tasks, ~151K LoC, ~2000 source and test files, 1331 expert-written tests; even strongest current agents achieve <10% behavioral success; compile-success mirage — Claude reported 29/30 successful builds while only 22 actually built; failure modes span build systems, deployment environments, dependency injection, databases, endpoints, assertions, infrastructure, Docker inconsistencies, port connectivity, Maven tooling; GitHub github.com/scarfbench/scarfbench, leaderboard scarfbench.info, dataset huggingface.co/datasets/ibm-research/ScarfBench

Beyond expert users: agents should help users construct preferences, not just elicit them / CoShop (Irena Saracay / Ludwig Schmidt / Carlos Guestrin) — attacks hidden assumption in interactive-agent design that users arrive with well-formed preferences; draws on Information Economics Search / Experience / Credence framework to formalize CoPref, in which users often don't know what they want and agent's job is to expand user's understanding of option space; CoShop is interactive benchmark for recommender-style tasks where user lacks domain expertise; no frontier agent exceeds 56% accuracy across five turns; named failure mode is agents re-ask clarifying questions about pre-existing preferences instead of expanding user's knowledge

OSWorld 2.0: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks (36 authors, eq-contrib Mengqi Yuan / Zilong Zhou / Xinzhuang Xiong; also Frederic Sala / Yu Su / Siva Reddy / Tao Yu) — 108 long-horizon CUA workflows averaging 318 tool calls and 1.6 hours of human work each (vs ~30 tool calls in original OSWorld); Claude Opus 4.8 (max thinking) reaches 20.6% binary completion / 54.8% partial score at 500 steps, GPT-5.5 plateaus near 13% (more token-efficient, doesn't close gap); named failure modes: lose track of constraints, miss mid-task information, struggle when task hinges on hidden state to recover; HF Daily Papers leading at 104 upvotes

VISTA / LLM Agents Are Latent Context Managers (Binyan Xu / Haitao Li / Kehuan Zhang) — coins the proprioceptively blind frame for context management; argues capable models already have latent policy but lack interface to see per-block token usage / recency / access history; training-free, model-agnostic layer represents working memory as typed addressable blocks + runtime dashboard + recoverable full-fidelity archive; on LOCA-Bench (1M-scale), BrowseComp-Plus (100K-scale), GAIA (10K-scale), same untrained interface transfers across four backbones; lifts Gemini-3-Flash 22.7% → 50.7% on LOCA-Bench; lift grows with context pressure; ablations confirm dashboard matters beyond archive/recovery alone

Neural Procedural Memory / Empowering LLM Agents with Implicit Activation Steering (Chengfeng Zhao / Yuqiao Tan / Shizhu He / Yequan Wang / Jun Zhao / Kang Liu) — names text-action disconnect failure of RAG-based procedural memory (model reads instruction without activating mechanisms that execute task); training-free framework distills procedural skills from historical contrastive experiences into steering vectors in activation space; across four agent benchmarks performs comparably to explicit-instruction baselines; combining implicit steering with explicit workflows is strictly better than either alone; representational analysis shows steering vectors encode consistent task logic forming organized structures in activation space

MemDelta: Controlled Baselines and Hidden Confounds in Agent Memory Evaluation (Kuan Wang) — controlled evaluation protocol on LongMemEval-S (500 questions, 50+ sessions, three model families); (1) verbatim RAG matches full-context on GPT-4o-mini (47.2% vs 49.8%, p=0.34) but ranking reverses across families (Gemini gains +14pp from full context, Sonnet gains +31pp from RAG); (2) swapping embedding model alone shifts accuracy ±6.2pp (n=500, p=0.004); Mem0 beats MiniLM-RAG by +11pp but underperforms cloud RAG; (3) agent self-memory underperforms basic retrieval 42% vs 47%; (4) Mem0 matches cloud RAG on 2 of 6 question types (n=88, 72.7% vs 73.9%, p=1.0) at 50x cost; prescribes fixed embedding model across comparisons, stratify by family, report write-path costs

Agents-A1 / Scaling the Horizon Not the Parameters (Lei Bai / Zongsheng Cao / Yang Chen + 47 others, InternScience) — 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model matching trillion-parameter Kimi-K2.6 / DeepSeek-V4-pro on long-horizon agent benchmarks; long-horizon knowledge-action infrastructure produces trajectories averaging 45K tokens; three-stage recipe — full-domain SFT → domain-level RL teachers → Multi-Teacher Domain-Routed On-Policy Distillation with Salient Vocabulary Alignment fusing six domains into one student; SEAL-0 56.4, IFBench 80.6, HiPhO 46.4, FrontierScience-Olympiad 79.0, MolBench-Bind 56.8, SciCode 44.3, HLE 47.6, BrowseComp 75.5; weights open-sourced at huggingface.co/collections/InternScience/agents-a1 + github.com/InternScience/Agents-A1

Entity Binding Failures in Tool-Augmented Agents (Rahul Suresh Babu / Shashank Indukuri) — formalizes wrong-entity errors as distinct failure mode from tool selection; agent picks the right tool, fires it against wrong external entity (email to wrong Alex, update wrong CRM row, reply in wrong thread); across 60 tasks × 5 model backends × 6 tool-use approaches: tool selection accuracy 0.0% error, entity binding failure rates 24.0–26.0% in action-oriented baselines; proposes entity-resolution preconditions, confidence-based binding, clarification queries; entity-aware safeguards eliminate wrong-entity errors but raise deferral rate

Minority Sentinel: When to Overturn Majority Voting in Multi-Agent LLM Debates (Chuan He / Zebin Chen / Zhengyi Yang / Shaobo Qiao / Mingchen Ju / Jiate Liu / Dong Wen / Guanfeng Liu) — Multi-Agent Debate + Majority Voting rests on Condorcet Jury Theorem assumption of independent errors; modern LLMs share pretraining corpora so errors are heavily correlated → majority systematically suppresses correct minorities (Minority Truth); across three heterogeneous LLMs × six benchmarks ~25% of divergent cases have minority correct (10pp theoretical recovery margin); lightweight non-LLM meta-classifier (LightGBM on multi-dimensional debate fingerprint) achieves 81.2% Flip Precision with positive Net Gain across all six datasets and 20 random seeds; LLM-as-Judge baseline yields negative Net Gain despite higher recall — flip safety not recovery volume determines intervention value

Always-OnAgents: A Survey of Persistent Memory, State, and Governance in LLM Agents (Tianyu Ding / Aditya Nannapaneni / Bingfan Liu / Ling Zhang — Cornell) — first systematic survey of persistent-state agent systems covering 435 works; encompasses retrievable memories, task ledgers, permissions, credentials, commitments, provenance/audit records, shared state, triggers, externally committed effects; six diagnostic axes (authority, scope, mutability, provenance, recoverability, actionability) + nine-stage lifecycle (writing → validating → organizing → retrieving → acting upon → updating → forgetting → auditing → rollback); headline observation: field overwhelmingly emphasizes accumulating and retrieving state, underweights governance / recovery / relinquishment; introduces Always-On Evaluation Protocol (AOEP-v0) scoring state mutation and recovery obligations not just answer quality

Supersede: Diagnosing and Training the Memory-Update Gap in LLM Agents (Vedant Patel) — isolates knowledge-update failure mode on LongMemEval supersession subset; bounded self-maintained memory drops gpt-5.4 from 92% → 77% (paired McNemar p<0.005); over 24x conversation growth accuracy collapses 68% → 28%; doubling memory budget yields no recovery (28% → 28%, n=25) — bottleneck is update policy not storage capacity; GRPO on Qwen2.5-3B on supersession environment nearly doubles held-out unseen-conversation supersession (9.0% → 16.7%); code, env, model, dataset open-sourced

Delayed Verification Destabilizes Multi-Agent LLM Belief: Instability Thresholds and Optimal Corrector Placement (Igor Itkin) — formalizes multi-agent verifier loops as delayed consensus on a graph with grounded corrector nodes; spectral analysis yields closed-form stability thresholds; worst regime is when communication delay = verification delay; at delay=2 critical verifier strength is inverse golden ratio (1/φ ≈ 0.618); supermodular placement objective enables greedy (1-1/e)-approximation; validated on 5 open models with predicted oscillation patterns; grounded factual answering eliminates instability — effect specific to signed-belief tasks; 20 pages, 5 figures

ATOD: Annealed Turn-aware On-policy Distillation (Qitai Tan / Zefang Zong / Yang Li / Peng Chen) — anneals imitation→RL on shared trajectory budget; Turn-level Disagreement-Uncertainty Reweighting upweights critical decision turns where teacher-student divergence is highest; ALFWorld + WebShop + Search-QA: +3.03 pts avg success vs on-policy distillation baseline, +23.62 pts vs GRPO baseline; surpasses corresponding teacher models by +2.16 pts across three student sizes

Gemini 3.5 Flash Computer Use built-in tool (Google DeepMind, Jun 26 2026) — computer use as first-party tool in Gemini API; cross-browser/mobile/desktop with one API call; Google claims best-yet OSWorld (number not in post — ledger has 78.4 OSWorld-Verified from [arxiv:2606.24515]); first-party safeguards: required-confirmation on sensitive actions + automatic task termination on prompt-injection detection; available via Gemini API (ai.google.dev), Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (GCP console), Browserbase-hosted demo; pricing and latency not specified

Internalizing the Future: A Unified Agentic Training Paradigm for World Model Planning (Xuan Zhang / Zhijian Zhou / Lingfeng Qiao / Yulei Qin / Ke Li / Xing Sun / Xiaoyu Tan / Chao Qu / Yuan Qi) — trains single autoregressive model to predict future states + estimate success probabilities (textual Q-value analog); identifies format-capability gap (naive SFT on traces with foresight tokens yields surface mimicry without action grounding); three-stage capability-first pipeline: World Model Agentic Mid-Training (WM-AMT) → Format-Eliciting SFT (FE-SFT) → Foresight-Conditioned RL (FC-RL); outperforms training baselines on search + math reasoning

QueenBee Planner: Skill-Evolving Communication Topologies for Token-Efficient LLM Multi-Agent Systems (Congjia Tian / Yuhang Yao / Jiaming Cui) — outer LLM planner generates temporal communication DAGs (who-sends-to-whom by round) refined across execution traces via Preserve/Modify/Avoid actions; safeguards include held-out acceptance gates, variance-aware credit, motif-level attribution, transfer trust, insight falsification, structural deduplication; Count-Frequency aggregation: best learned topology cuts RMSE from 12.53 → 7.87 while simultaneously reducing messages, model calls, and token cost; similar gains on Silo-Bench-style distributed coordination

Glite ARF: Verifier-Driven Research with Parallel LLM Coding Agents (Vassili Philippov / Pavel Katunin / Dmitry Andreev / Igor Ostanin / Anton Nikolaev) — open-source Python framework for parallel LLM coding agents on research projects; three-role split (human picks hypotheses, agents execute within fixed params, deterministic Python verifiers enforce process rules — task isolation, work immutability); BEA 2026 Vocabulary-Difficulty Task: 1st place closed track / 2nd place open track across Spanish/German/Mandarin; +29.9% closed / +35.9% open RMSE reduction; 273 tasks across 146 runs / 129 feature sets; ~$498 total LLM spend; ~1% framework wall-clock overhead

RiVER / Reinforcement Learning without Ground-Truth Solutions can Improve LLMs (Yingyu Lin / Qiyue Gao / Nikki Lijing Kuang / Xunpeng Huang / Kun Zhou / Tongtong Liang / Zhewei Yao / Yi-An Ma / Yuxiong He) — trains LLMs via group-relative RL on score-based optimization tasks using deterministic execution feedback as continuous-valued supervision; addresses scale dominance (uncalibrated score magnitudes distort updates) + frequency dominance (suboptimal solutions repeatedly sampled outweigh rare strong ones); calibrated reward shaping with instance-wise comparisons emphasizing top-ranked solvers; trained on 12 AtCoder Heuristic Contest tasks; Qwen3-8B + GLM-Z1-9B-0414; ALE rating-rank +8.9%/+9.4%; LiveCodeBench +2.4pp; USACO +3.5pp

LMs as Task-Specific Knowledge Bases: An Interpretability Analysis (Amit Elhelo / Amir Globerson / Mor Geva) — behavioral + mechanistic analysis; facts acquired on one task frequently fail to co-emerge on others during training; parameter localization shows distinct parameter subsets underlie different tasks for the same fact; chain-of-thought reasoning draws part of its effectiveness from engaging task-specific parameters beyond those tied to the evaluation task; what the model knows and how it is asked are intertwined in parameter space; undermines knowledge base analogy

HyperDFlash / MHC-Aligned Block Speculative Decoding with Gated Residual Reduction for DeepSeek-V4 (Luxi Lin / Shuang Peng / Rui Ma / Junhao Hua / Shuwei Fan / Zhengda Qin / Qiang Wang / Hongjian Sun / Fangmin Chen / Songwei Liu) — native MTP module draft accuracy degrades sharply at later positions from error accumulation; DFlash one-pass block drafting cannot directly adapt due to MHC multi-path residual stream feature misalignment; pre-collapse residual states as exclusive conditioning signal preserves multi-path structural info; gated residual reducer inherits params from built-in hyper-connection head (3 orders of magnitude fewer params than generic linear compressor); targeted KL distillation on LM-head; substantial accepted-draft-length + decoding speedup over MTP and vanilla DFlash on math/code/conversational benchmarks

Multilingual Reasoning Cascades Need More Context (Arnav Mazumder / Dengjia Zhang / Shuyue Stella Li / Yulia Tsvetkov / Niyati Bafna) — translation cascades for multilingual reasoning are competitive but structurally lossy at each stage boundary; training-free context-aware cascade additionally provides original-language question + English-translated question + English reasoning trace to final translation module; 9 multilingual benchmarks x 3 backbones x 285 high/mid/low-resource languages; strong gains on open-ended generation across models and resource regimes; ablation: original-language question carries most of the beneficial context

Reasoning Quality Emerges Early: Data Curation for Reasoning Models (Hongyi Henry Jin / Wenhan Yang / Meysam Ghaffari / Carlos Morato / Baharan Mirzasoleiman) — diverse and challenging reasoning SFT examples identifiable from initial reasoning tokens; difficult problems reliably detectable from loss of first 100 reasoning tokens at a randomly perturbed checkpoint of the pretrained model; examples with similar loss patterns over first 1k tokens across small number of perturbed checkpoints provably induce similar gradients; Qwen2.5-7B + Llama3.1-8B on M23K medical + OpenThoughts-Math; outperforms baselines by up to 1.7%; 91% more token-efficient curation

PEEU + TDHAF / Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning (Tianyi Men / Zhuoran Jin / Pengfei Cao / Yubo Chen / Kang Liu / Jun Zhao — ACL 2026 Main) — small open MLLMs autonomously explore environments to discover experiences; hindsight experience synthesizes strictly aligned high-level training data; Task Decomposition Hierarchical Analysis Framework examines compositional generalization across three granularity levels; mastering foundational skills does not guarantee higher-level planning competence; 7B model achieves 30.6% accuracy on real-world GUI benchmarks, outperforms Qwen2.5-VL-32B baseline

Diagnosing Task Insensitivity in Language Agents (Jingyu Liu / Xiaopeng Wu / Kehan Chen / Chuan Yu / Yong Liu) — identifies task insensitivity as key OOD failure mode: agents apply patterns learned during training and fail to solve task at hand; models continue with actions aligned to original task even when instruction is semantically corrupted; replacing task description with similar-but-distinct task often produces same action; accompanied by consistent training-time attention drift away from task tokens and toward local observations suggesting optimization bias toward shortcuts; proposes Task-Perturbed NLL Optimization lightweight contrastive regularizer encouraging action dependence on task instruction; improves task sensitivity + OOD generalization + attention stability

Robust-TO / Confidence-Aware Tool Orchestration for Robust Video Understanding (Yangfan He / Yujin Choi / Jaehong Yoon — NTU Singapore) — Blind Trust Problem: video reasoning models suffer 15-30pp accuracy drops under realistic perturbations while unaware visual evidence has degraded; agentic framework organizes heterogeneous visual tools under unified evidence interface returning {prediction, temporal grounding, calibrated reliability score}; reliability-relevance score for frame selection per tool sub-query; three-tier (high/medium/low) synthesis; confidence-cost GRPO reward jointly optimizes correctness + reliability + efficiency; clean accuracy 56.4% (+10.6pp over best open-source, beats Gemini-2.5-Pro 46.2%); corrupted-input accuracy 54.3% (+5.8pp); smallest clean-to-corrupted drop of all methods

CARVE / Content-Aware Recurrent with Value Efficiency for Chunk-Parallel Linear Attention (Sayak Dutta) — recurrent models must forget to remember but GDN-2 erase gate sees only arriving token not the memory being modified; performs erasure on key axis not value axis to maintain mathematical validity for WY-form triangular chunk solver; reuses recurrent output tensor as content signal for erase gate; replaces per-value write-gate projections with single scalar per head; 1.3B params / 100B tokens; WikiText perplexity 15.72 (-0.18 vs GDN-2 at 4.5-sigma); leads recurrent baselines on 9 commonsense reasoning benchmarks; SOTA on RULER retrieval probes; 0.4% throughput overhead, 13% lower peak memory, 19% fewer parameters

Nemotron 3 Ultra NVFP4 Checkpoint (NVIDIA Developer Blog, 2026-06-26; Seonghee Lee / Sachin Beldona / Carlo del Mundo / Chris Hoge / Trenton Starkey) — 550B-param model compressed BF16 1,121 GB -> NVFP4 352.3 GB (3.2x compression); NVFP4 = 4-bit float format on Blackwell with 8 representable positive values (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6); decode-heavy throughput up to 5.9x vs GLM-5.1 754B FP4; 98.5% median accuracy recovery vs BF16 across benchmarks; identifies 5.03 BPE as compression-vs-accuracy sweet spot

MemStrata / Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory: Eliminating Stale-Fact Errors for AI Agents (Neeraj Yadav) — bi-temporal retrieval memory; (subject,relation,object) supersession rule retires stale values via deterministic ledger; cosine similarity 0.59 AUROC on contradicted-fact vs duplicate (barely above chance); evolving knowledge accuracy 0.95-1.00 vs RAG 0.20-0.47; stale-fact error rate 15-40% -> ~0%; retrieval latency ~2.1s vs 16-18s for LLM-rerank baselines; code + evaluation datasets + marker-free protocol released

JERP / Joint Learning of Experiential Rules and Policies for LLM Agents (Shicheng Ye, Chao Yu) — couples long-term experiential rule pool with policy on the same interaction trajectories; both updated per episode by comparing current vs successful reference; AlfWorld + WebShop consistent decision gains over rules-only and policy-only baselines

InfoKV / Information-Aware KV Cache Compression for Long Reasoning (Jushi Kai, Zhuiri Xiao, Alexandra Birch, Zhouhan Lin) — Forward Influence metric measures how compressed tokens affect distant future contexts; attention-selected tokens primarily near-future influence, high predictive uncertainty tokens substantially stronger distant-future influence; combines entropy + attention scores during prefill+decode; consistently outperforms attention-only baselines on Llama-3.1 / Llama-3.2 / DeepSeek-R1 long-context reasoning

PersistentKV / Page-Aware Decode Scheduling for Long-Context LLM Serving (Muhammad Ahmed) — native block-table decode attention engine for GQA; schedules work by KV-head group with tile reuse across query heads; native page tables + compact workqueue + executes only non-empty row-KV-head-sequence-split tasks; RTX 3060 FP16 Hq=32 Hkv=8 d=128 page=16: 1.063-1.265x B8 bimodal/uniform/Zipf, 1.399x B1 bucketed workloads; 7-page workshop paper

Frozen Multi-Token Prediction on Gemini Nano (Pixel 9/10) — Google Research blog 2026-06-26; retrofits dense transformer MTP head onto frozen pre-trained Gemini Nano v3 backbone; MTP head cross-attends directly to main model's frozen KV cache (zero-copy late-exit design); predicts ~2 additional tokens per inference pass; 50%+ speedup on Pixel 9, 130MB memory savings vs standalone drafter, up to 55% token-acceptance improvement on predictable text; bit-for-bit identical to main model output

Thinking to Recall / How Reasoning Unlocks Parametric Knowledge in LLMs (Zorik Gekhman, Jonathan Herzig, Google Research; blog 2026-06-24 linking arxiv:2603.09906) — two mechanisms enabling reasoning to help single-hop factual recall: (1) computational buffer = extra forward passes for latent computation refining internal state; (2) factual priming = generates topically related facts as semantic warm-up (spreading activation analog); Gemini-2.5 Flash/Pro + Qwen3-32B on SimpleQA Verified + EntityQuestions; reasoning-on recovers answers virtually unrecoverable with reasoning off; hallucinated intermediate facts significantly degrade final accuracy

Where Do CoT Training Gains Land in LLM-Based Agents? (Jingyu Liu / Zhiwen Wang / Yuxin Jing / Huanyu Zhou / Yong Liu) — CoT training does not widen advantage of CoT-action over prompt-action; only improves prompt-action quality; later checkpoints decreased likelihood of revising action based on generated reasoning; proposes selective action-token-supervision masking for OOD generalization

OpenRCA 2.0 / From Outcome Labels to Causal Process Supervision (Aoyang Fang et al.) — PAVE step-wise labeling protocol annotates causal propagation paths rather than just root causes; 500 cross-system instances; outcome-only 76.0% identify correct root-cause service vs process-supervision 61.5% ground in verified causal path; exact root-cause recovery 20.7% across 11 frontier LLMs; fault-injection-driven causal-chain reconstruction; work in progress

OPID / On-Policy Skill Distillation for Agentic RL (Shuo Yang / Jinyang Wu / Zhengxi Lu / Yuhao Shen / Fan Zhang / Lang Feng / Shuai Zhang / Haoran Luo / Zheng Lian / Zhengqi Wen / Jianhua Tao) — extracts hierarchical skills from completed on-policy trajectories (episode-level workflows + step-level critical decisions); critical-first routing selects skill guidance and injects into interaction history; policy re-scores under original + skill-augmented contexts giving token-level self-distillation advantage combined with outcome advantage; ALFWorld / WebShop / Search-QA improvements in success, sample efficiency, robustness vs outcome-only RL baselines; code released

Memory Depth, Not Memory Access: Selective Parametric Consolidation for Long-Running Language Agents / EVAF (Haoliang Han) — argues retrieval is access only; long-running agents also need durable goal-conditioned tendencies in a small parametric store; surprise- and valence-gated LoRA consolidation; loop-drift protocol tests recovery after parametric store reload; tested GPT-2 / TinyLlama / Mistral-7B; retrieval accuracy 0.956-0.973 on factual recall; EVAF 0.812-0.904 on goal persistence and post-unload recovery; parametric efficiency 2-3 writes per 200 events

Semantic Early-Stopping for Iterative LLM Agent Loops (Sahil Shrivastava) — judge-free stopping rule halting when consecutive draft embeddings stop changing in meaning; machine-checked theoretical guarantees + evaluation protocol replaying policies over cached outputs; HotpotQA: -38% operational tokens vs fixed-iteration baseline at parity quality (delta-IS=-0.004, p=0.81); quality-gated variant counterproductive due to per-round judging cost; oracle best-round selection +0.115 IS advantage over all practical policies (p~4e-11); open-source impl + reproducible harness

Co-Failure Ceiling on Routing/Voting/Mixture-of-Agents (Josef Chen) — defines beta = rate at which every model in ensemble wrong on same query; proves accuracy bounded by 1-beta; 67 frontier models / 21 providers; math beta=0.052 (2.5x higher than Gaussian copula prediction 0.023), code execution beta=0.079, GPQA-Diamond beta=0.127 when reformatted MCQ->free-response; gains come from models failing on different questions not from adding more models; heterogeneous low-correlation ensembles outperform Self-MoA at matched quality

The Verification Horizon: No Silver Bullet for Coding Agent Rewards (Binghai Wang / Chenlong Zhang / Dayiheng Liu / Jiajun Zhang / Jiawei Chen / Mouxiang Chen / Rongyao Fang / Siyuan Zhang / Xuwu Wang / Yuheng Jing / Zeyao Ma / Zeyu Cui — Qwen/Alibaba) — examines four reward constructions (test verifiers / rubric verifiers / user-as-verifier / automated agent verifiers); core thesis no fixed reward function remains effective as policy capability grows, verification must co-evolve with the generator; intent underspecification and reward hacking as structural challenges; significant gains across multiple internal and public benchmarks; concrete numbers not in abstract

Why Multi-Step Tool-Use RL Collapses and How Supervisory Signals Fix It (Yupu Hao / Zhuoran Jin / Huanxuan Liao / Kang Liu / Jun Zhao — CASIA) — diagnoses catastrophic collapse in multi-step tool-use RL: performance abruptly drops and tool-invocation structure fails mid-training; mechanism is unexpected probability spikes in control tokens not lost capability; tests off-policy supervision, hint-based guidance, erroneous-example supervision; interleaving SFT with RL substantially improves stability; OOD degradation persists; code at hypasd-art/Tool-RL-Box

SKILL-DISCO: Distilling and Compiling Agent Traces into Reusable Procedural Skills (Zhongxin Guo / Danrui Qi / Hanwen Gu / Peng Cheng / Yongqiang Xiong) — agents repeatedly solve similar task instances from scratch; mines reusable procedural subgraphs from successful traces and compiles into callable skills the agent invokes as composite tools; ALFWorld + WebArena; improves success rates and reduces agent turns across benchmarks and model scales; concrete deltas not in abstract

The Capability Frontier: Benchmarks Miss 82% of Model Performance (Bradley Fowler / Ryan Smith / Daniel Thi Graviet / William Myers / Joshua Greaves / Narmeen Fatimah Oozeer / Antia Garcia / Philip Quirke / Amirali Abdullah / Fazl Barez / Shriyash Kaustubh Upadhyay) — Capability Frontier framework measures optimal achievable accuracy at each cost level under (a) single-model bias correction (b) single-run sampling correction; 21 LLMs x 16 benchmarks (coding/reasoning/medicine/factuality/instruction-following/agentic); 54% error-rate reduction from single-model bias correction; 82% error-rate reduction when also correcting single-run sampling; 85% cost reduction to match SOTA accuracy; traditional benchmarks systematically underestimate collective LLM capabilities

Ask Don't Judge / BINEVAL (Sangwoo Cho / Kushal Chawla / Pengshan Cai / Zefang Liu / Chenyang Zhu / Shi-Xiong Zhang / Sambit Sahu) — decomposes LLM-as-judge into atomic binary questions auto-generated via meta-prompt then aggregates per-question verdicts into multi-dimensional scores; SummEval / Topical-Chat / QAGS matches or exceeds UniEval / G-Eval baselines; especially strong on factual-consistency QAGS; better matches human score distributions than prior LLM judges; improved iterative prompt optimization on summarization + IFBench; ICML 2026 Workshop on Compositional Learning

Autoformalization of Agent Instructions into Policy-as-Code (Adam Mondl / Matthew Maisel / John H. Brock) — autoformalization pipeline translates agent prompts / MCP tool descriptions / NL policy documents into formally verified policies in Cedar Policy Language via LLM-driven loop; MedAgentBench: autoformalized policies achieve substantially greater coverage of source NL specification vs hand-coded symbolic enforcement from prior work; probabilistic safety can't give guarantees Cedar evaluator can; ICML 2026 Workshop on Agents in the Wild (AIWILD)

CUGA FLO / Process Harness for Uplifting Legacy Workflows to Agentic BPM (Fabiana Fournier / Lior Limonad — IBM Research) — process harness wraps policy-governed agentic layer around existing deterministic workflow engine without replacing it; Task-Decision-Flow (TDF) model with three policy-governed agent types (TaskAgent / DecisionAgent / FlowAgent) invoked at designated control points; loan-approval workflow demonstration with regulatory-override behavior; reconciles imperative requirements (deterministic execution) with normative requirements (agentic autonomy at policy-framed control points); design paper, no quantitative benchmarks; CUGA follow-up

Which Tokens Does a Hybrid Model Predict Better? (Kyle Wiggers / Ai2Comms for Allen Institute for AI) — controlled comparison Olmo 3 (7B transformer) vs Olmo Hybrid (7B attention+recurrence) trained on identical data/tokenizer/recipe; token-level loss decomposition shows hybrid wins on content words (nouns/verbs/adjectives loss gap ~0.04) + state-tracking tokens (pronouns); transformers win on verbatim repetition (hybrid advantage approaches zero) + bracket-matching (closing braces); additional 1B-parameter triple (transformer/hybrid/pure RNN) for finer analysis; single aggregate loss obscures architectural strengths

Metis: Bridging Text and Code Memory for Self-Evolving Agents (Zijie Dai, Siuhin He, Hui Li, Qihui Zhou, Jiajun Li, Mingcong Song, Guoping Long, Hongjie Si, Xin Yao, Lin Zhang, James Cheng, Xiao Yan) — controlled comparison of text- vs code-based memory representations followed by hierarchical dual-representation system; text memory stores execution plans / environment facts / common pitfalls while recurring patterns selectively promoted to executable tools; AppWorld evaluation: +20.6 pts task accuracy over ReAct baseline at -22.8% execution cost; outperforms other self-evolving agent systems across accuracy, efficiency, and construction cost

EDV / Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap: An Execute-Distill-Verify Paradigm for Agentic Experience Learning (Shiding Zhu, Yudi Qi, Yajie Wang, Jiaze Li, Chao Song, Yaorui Shi, Yibo Miao, Hanqi Gao, Kai Zhang) — identifies self-confirmation trap (single-agent experience learning reinforces own mistakes); three-role decomposition: Execute (multiple heterogeneous agents in parallel) -> Distill (dedicated third-party agent comparatively analyzes trajectories) -> Verify (executor group validates by consensus before memory write); consistent improvements on tau2-bench, Mind2Web, MMTB; code at shidingz/EDV

Reinforcement Learning for Computer-Use Agents with Autonomous Evaluation (Marta Sumyk, Oleksandr Kosovan) — GLOW @ IJCAI 2026; VLM-as-judge compares final screenshot to instruction emitting binary completion signal; models as noisy binary reward channel and derives noise-corrected estimator for PPO; +12.6 pts over zero-shot, +5.1 pts over raw evaluator fine-tuning across macOSWorld / Windows Agent Arena / OSWorld; noise correction is the actual contribution (VLM-as-judge tried before; explicit noise model makes PPO-stable)

Bayesian Control for Coding Agents (Theodore Papamarkou, Vladislav Smirnov, Viktor Mazanov, Artem Vazhentsev, Preslav Nakov, Timothy Baldwin, Artem Shelmanov) — reframes coding-agent tool orchestration as cost-sensitive sequential hypothesis testing; controller maintains Bayesian belief about code correctness and adaptively decides whether to gather evidence / refine / verify / stop; six code generators × nine benchmarks; Bayesian belief state outperforms token-probability and raw tool-success baselines for uncertainty quantification; largest gains when verification is expensive but informative

ToolPrivBench / When Lower Privileges Suffice: Investigating Over-Privileged Tool Selection in LLM Agents (Kaiyue Yang, Yuyan Bu, Jingwei Yi, Yuchi Wang, Biyu Zhou, Juntao Dai, Songlin Hu, Yaodong Yang) — defines and measures over-privileged tool selection; eight domains, five risk patterns, tests initial selection + escalation behavior; over-privileged selection common across mainstream agents; prompt-level controls fail under transient tool failures (agent escalates when low-privilege call errors); general safety training does NOT transfer to least-privilege decisions; proposes privilege-aware post-training defense; code at AISafetyHub/agent-tool-selection-bias

Privacy-Preserving RAG via Multi-Agent Semantic Rewriting (Yuanhe Zhao, Tianyu Zhang, Huafei Xing, Derek F. Wong, Jianbin Li, Tao Fang) — Elsevier Information Processing & Management accepted; three-agent framework (privacy extraction + semantic analysis + reconstruction) sanitizes RAG context as offline preprocessing; LLaMA-3-8B leak instances 144 -> 1 under targeted attacks; BLEU-1 0.122 vs SAGE 0.117 (slight quality gain); zero added latency at inference time; ChatDoctor + Wiki-PII across six LLMs; code at foursoils/Privacy-Preserving-RAG

Autodata: An Agentic Data Scientist to Create High Quality Synthetic Data (Ilia Kulikov, Chenxi Whitehouse, Tianhao Wu, Yixin Nie, Swarnadeep Saha, Eryk Helenowski, Weizhe Yuan, Olga Golovneva, Jack Lanchantin, Yoram Bachrach, Jakob Foerster, Xian Li, Han Fang, Sainbayar Sukhbaatar, Jason Weston — Meta FAIR) — Agentic Self-Instruct paradigm: agent system functions as autonomous data scientist generating synthetic training+eval datasets, can be meta-optimized to improve own data-creation; CS research / legal reasoning / mathematical reasoning with objects; improvements over classical synthetic dataset creation methods, meta-optimization gives larger uplift; concrete benchmark numbers not in abstract

Grading the Grader: Lessons from Evaluating an Agentic Data Analysis System (Tian Zheng, Kai-Tai Hsu) — applied LAMBDA to 153 QRData tasks; three-layer grading cascade (regex + LLM-lenient + human snippet inspection) distinguishes real disagreement from grading artifacts; both automated graders achieve 100% observed precision (0 false positives / 70 cases); lenient grader 97% recall vs human; keyword-anchored extraction +60 pts to strict grader recall; iterative nudging raises grading success 36% -> 97%; lenient-pass 16% -> 46%

CUGA (Configurable Generalist Agent): Apache-2.0 production agent harness from IBM Research with 24 working single-file FastAPI example apps — handles planning, state, tool orchestration, declarative guardrails (Intent Guards, Tool Approval, Playbooks), multi-agent delegation, model-agnostic provider switching, three reasoning modes (Fast / Balanced / Accurate), interchangeable tool layer (OpenAPI / MCP / LangChain); examples include IBM Cloud advisor, Paper Scout, Wiki Dive, PDF/audio/video document RAG, Ouroboros (seven-agent lead-gen), Meetup Finder (Playwright browser automation); pip install cuga; repos cuga-project/cuga-agent + cuga-project/cuga-apps; open-source analog to Claude Tag

Kog Laneformer 2B: The Latency-First Model Behind Kog Inference Engine (Kog AI) — kogai/laneformer-2b-it; 2.3B-parameter instruction-tuned coding model trained from scratch with novel Delayed Tensor Parallelism 8-lane architecture; 15 decoder layers with Grouped-Query Attention (32 query heads / 16 KV heads); Sliding Window Attention on 10 layers; 4096-token context; Apache-2.0 model code (Llama-2 community license on tokenizer); ~4T pretrain + ~2T mid-train + ~210M instruction-tune tokens, ~21 days × 192 H100s; HumanEval+ 45.1% / MBPP+ 51.6% (below Qwen2.5-Coder-7B's ~80%); 3000 tok/s on 8×MI300X, 2100 tok/s on 8×H200; latency is the selling point, not quality

Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System? (Wei Zhou, Xuanhe Zhou, Shaokun Han, Hongming Xu, Guoliang Li, Zhiyu Li, Feiyu Xiong, Fan Wu) — systematic data-management evaluation of 12 memory systems + 2 baselines across 5 workloads / 11 datasets; four-module decomposition (representation+storage, extraction, retrieval+routing, maintenance); no single architecture dominates — effectiveness depends on workload-bottleneck alignment; localized maintenance > global reorganization on cost-performance; code at OpenDataBox/MemoryData

Governed Shared Memory for Multi-Agent LLM Systems / MemClaw + ArgusFleet (Margalit, Cohen-Inger, Avram, Taig, Margalit — BGU+IBM inferred) — formalizes fleet-memory problem with four failure modes (unauthorized leakage, stale propagation, contradiction persistence, provenance collapse) + four primitives (scoped retrieval, temporal supersession, provenance tracking, policy-governed propagation); MemClaw production multi-tenant service eval'd via ArgusFleet harness; 100% reconstruction of depth-4 derivation chains, zero cross-fleet leakage, sub-second per-hop provenance; discovered two production failures — sub-tenant scope bypass on direct GET-by-id (disclosed+remediated), pipeline-ordering conflict where sync near-duplicate gate rejects contradictory writes before async detector evaluates; thesis: long-context retrieval alone insufficient for production multi-agent memory

ReM-MoA: Reasoning Memory Sustains Mixture-of-Agents Scaling (Heng Ping, Arijit Bhattacharjee, Peiyu Zhang, Shixuan Li, Wei Yang, Ali Jannesari, Nesreen Ahmed, Paul Bogdan) — prior MoA degrades/plateaus/saturates with depth; ReM-MoA adds Ranked Reasoning Memory (Reviewer Agent comparative ranking of traces from all layers) + Curated Diversified Memory Routing (distinct success/failure trace mixes per agent); optional multi-domain Reviewer distillation pipeline pulls frontier-model supervision; 5 reasoning benchmarks (math, formal logic, code, knowledge, commonsense); advantage widens with depth; positioned as 'key missing mechanism for scalable multi-agent inference'

MEMPROBE: Probing Long-Term Agent Memory via Hidden User-State Recovery (Enze Ma, Yufan Zhou, Wei-Chieh Huang, Jie Yang, Huanhuan Ma, Zixuan Wang, Chengze Li, Chunyu Miao, Philip S. Yu, Zhen Wang) — evaluates memory as auditable post-interaction artifact rather than via downstream task success; 50 simulated users × 31 hidden dimensions = 1,550 recovery targets; 5 memory systems tested; task completion nearly saturates (even for memoryless baseline) while category-balanced recovery sits ~0.6 and drops further under top-k; demonstrates that successful assistance and recoverable memory are distinct capabilities

Qwen-AgentWorld: Language World Models for General Agents (Qwen team, 33 authors led by Yuxin Zuo, Zikai Xiao, Li Sheng, Fei Huang) — Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B + 397B-A17B trained on 10M+ environment trajectories across 7 domains; three-stage training (CPT inject world modeling capability, SFT activate next-state-prediction reasoning, RL with hybrid rubric+rule rewards); AgentWorldBench from real interactions of 5 frontier models on 9 benchmarks; claims to significantly outperform existing frontier models; two deployment paradigms — (a) decoupled simulator for agentic RL (beats real-env training alone), (b) world-model training as warm-up for downstream agent fine-tunes (improves across 7 agentic benchmarks); 35B-A3B variant is M5 Max-local-fit

NatureBench: Can Coding Agents Match the Published SOTA of Nature-Family Papers? (Yuru Wang, Lejun Cheng, Yuxin Zuo, Sihang Zeng, Bingxiang He, et al. — 17 authors, Frontis AI) — 90 tasks distilled from peer-reviewed Nature-family publications; NatureGym auto-builds per-task containerized environments addressing env-fragmentation; strict web-search-disabled protocol; best of 10 frontier agent configurations matches SOTA on 17.8% of tasks (g>0.1 criterion); agents succeed via methodological translation (converting scientific tasks into supervised prediction problems) not invention; failures dominated by wrong method choice + insufficient compute budget, not task misunderstanding; benchmark + NatureGym pipeline + public leaderboard released

Block-GTQ: RoPE-Aware Bit Allocation for KV-Cache Quantization (Fengfeng Liang, Yuechen Zhang, Jiaya Jia — JIA-Lab) — RoPE decomposes key contribution into position-dependent 2D frequency blocks; Block-GTQ computes label-free per-block energy score and greedily allocates integer bit-widths by marginal gain; built on TurboQuant-MSE; per-layer MAE drops 32-80% at 2-3 b/dim K-only, wins all 367/367 layer comparisons vs uniform TQ-MSE; Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct K2V2: NIAH 70.6→97.4, LongBench-EN 36.87→53.31; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B AIME K3V2: 51.7/37.5 vs fp16 54.2/37.9 (uniform TQ-MSE: 0.0/0.0); Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct K3V3 on H800: 3.24x KV compression, 1.34x faster than fp16 FlashAttention2 at 128K, peak memory 56.31 GB→19.85 GB, feasible at 256K/512K where fp16 OOMs; code at JIA-Lab-research/blockgtq

SAFARI: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Fault Attribution via Active Investigation (Chenyang Zhu, Jiayu Yao, Kushal Chawla, Youbing Yin, Nathan Wolfe, Pengshan Cai, Jingyu Wu, Spencer Hong, Sangwoo Cho, Shi-Xiong Zhang, Daben Liu, Sambit Sahu, Erin Babinsky) — replaces full-trajectory-into-context with tool-augmented diagnostic loop; specialized tools to read+search trajectory segments + persistent Short-Term Memory for cross-turn reasoning; decouples diagnostic accuracy from native context window; +20% over SOTA on Who&When at 1M token budget, +19% on TRAIL GAIA subset at 25K budget; 0.58 precision when fault sits 5x beyond model's native context window (where traditional evaluators fail entirely)

OpenThoughts-Agent: Data Recipes for Agentic Models (OpenThoughts consortium, 50 authors — Negin Raoof lead; Richard Zhuang, Marianna Nezhurina, Etash Guha et al.) — fully open data-curation pipeline for training generalist agent models; 100+ controlled ablations across pipeline stages on task sources + diversity + mixing; 100K-example training set; Qwen3-32B fine-tune: 44.8% avg across seven agentic benchmarks (+3.9 pts over Nemotron-Terminal-32B 40.9%); outperforms alternative open datasets at every training size in compute-controlled comparisons; training sets + pipeline + experiment logs + models released at openthoughts.ai

Anthropic — Introducing Claude Tag (June 23, 2026) — Slack-native multi-user Claude agent on Opus 4.8; beta for Enterprise + Team plans; replaces Claude-in-Slack app over 30-day migration; scoped identities with separate memories per use case (admin-controlled tool+data access per channel); proactive 'ambient' mode flags relevant info across connected channels; multiplayer pickup (anyone in channel can continue); asynchronous autonomous work over extended periods; Anthropic reports their internal version writes 65% of product team's code

Self-Compacting Language Model Agents (Tianjian Li, Jingyu Zhang, William Jurayj, Xi Wang, Chuanyang Jin, Mehrdad Farajtabar, Eric Nalisnick, Daniel Khashabi — JHU + Apple) — SelfCompact gives the agent a compaction tool plus a decision rubric for when to invoke (at task completion or convergence, not mid-derivation); matches or surpasses fixed-interval summarization at 30–70% lower per-question cost; +18.1 pts on math, +5–9 pts on agentic search across six benchmarks and seven models; identifies meta-cognitive gap (unprompted models can't recognize context degradation; lightweight scaffolding closes it); no fine-tuning or external supervision

EvoEmbedding: Evolvable Representations for Long-Context Retrieval and Agentic Memory (Chang Nie, Chaoyou Fu, Junlan Feng, Caifeng Shan — Nanjing University) — Embedding model maintaining continuously-updated latent memory while processing sequential inputs; EvoTrain-180K dataset, memory-queue mechanism prevents representation collapse, segment-batching for 3.8x training acceleration; outperforms Qwen3-Embedding-8B and KaLM-Embedding-Gemma3-12B on long-context retrieval; generalizes to contexts 10x longer than training window; claims naive RAG with EvoEmbedding surpasses dedicated agentic memory systems — directly comparable to GateMem (arxiv:2606.18829) governance thesis and Recall (gh:raiyanyahya/recall) local-ledger thesis

PlanBench-XL: Evaluating Long-Horizon Planning of LLM Tool-Use Agents in Large-Scale Tool Ecosystems (Jiayu Liu, Qihan Lin, Cheng Qian, Rui Wang, Emre Can Acikgoz, Xiaocheng Yang, Jiateng Liu, Zhenhailong Wang, Xiusi Chen, Heng Ji, Dilek Hakkani-Tür — UIUC) — 327 retail tasks over 1,665 tools with blocking mechanism simulating missing/failing tool functions; evaluates iterative tool retrieval + intermediate evidence under retrieval-limited tool visibility; GPT-5.4 hits 51.90% standard but drops to 11.36% under severe blocking; agents struggle when errors lack explicit signals or recovery requires longer alternative tool sequences; formalizes silent-failure regime in MCP/tool agent stacks

OpenRath: Session-Centered Runtime State for Agent Systems (Fukang Wen, Zhijie Wang, Ruilin Xu) — PyTorch-inspired programming model for agent runtime; Session is central abstraction (records conversation, sandbox placement, lineage metadata, token usage, tool evidence) and is branchable, inspectable, replayable, backend-aware, composable; companion abstractions Sandbox, Tool, Agent, Memory, Workflow, Selector (Selector converts control flow into runtime-routed decisions); enables explicit fork/merge/replay without reconstructing state from external traces; evaluation deferred to future work — controlled runtime properties only

CLI-Universe: Towards Verifiable Task Synthesis Engine for Terminal Agents (Zhanbo Hua, Yifan Yao, Weihao Xie, Yongchi Zhao, Minghao Liu, Ruizhi Qiu, Zhewei Huang, Zun Wang, Yiyan Ji, Yunhai Ye, Letian Zhu, Xinping Lei, Han Li, Zhiyuan Ma, Zili Wang, Zhaoxiang Zhang, Jiaheng Liu — NJU-LINK Lab) — Systematic synthesis pipeline generates trajectories across multiple capability dimensions, grounds them in technical materials, verifies in Docker; ~2/3 candidates filtered; releases CLI-Universe-6K (6,000 verified trajectories); Qwen3-32B fine-tuned on it hits 33.4% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 — claimed SOTA for open models ≤32B, beats models an order of magnitude larger; Qwen3-32B Q4 fits comfortably on M5 Max 64GB unified memory

OpenAI Daybreak Expansion + Full GPT-5.5-Cyber + Patch the Planet (2026-06-22 product launch) — Full GPT-5.5-Cyber release sets SOTA on three defensive benchmarks: CyberGym 85.6% (vs 81.8% base GPT-5.5), ExploitGym 39.5% (vs 25.95%), SEC-bench Pro 69.8% (vs 63.1%); Patch the Planet co-founded with Trail of Bits ships open-source patching pipeline targeting cURL, Go, Python, Sigstore, pyca/cryptography (30+ projects committed); Codex Security plugin adds severity reports + attack-path tracing + codebase-specific patch generation; launch partners Accenture/Cisco/CrowdStrike/IBM/Okta/Palo Alto Networks/Wiz; first quantified-benchmark frontier release of a defensive coding agent

Oak: Version Control System for AI Coding Agents (Zach Geier + Adam Morse — HN front page 2026-06-22, 172 points) — Purpose-built VCS for autonomous coding agents; lazy filesystem-mount of remote repos (files hydrate on first access, no full clone); branch-per-task with description-as-squash-message; parallel tasks on separate mounts without .git corruption; content-defined chunking deduplicates across versions (single tensor change in 4GB file uploads only modified chunks); reports up to 95% lower median latency vs git on snapshots and large-file ops, initial snapshot 29.7s → 1.4s on many-small-files repos; oak export replays into standard git; source at oak.space/oak/oak, license not stated on landing page

DynamicMem: A Long-Horizon Memory Benchmark in Real-World Settings (Wenya Xie et al. incl. Vladimir Braverman, Ali Payani, Zirui Liu — 12 authors) — Simulates 15 months of activity per user across 16 applications (e-commerce/fitness/social), 2.2M tokens and 1,772 events per user on average, five quarterly checkpoints; systems must infer user attributes/habits/preferences from scattered implicit signals; three killer findings: (a) profile reconstruction degrades as history lengthens while service-task accuracy stays flat, (b) no system maintains stable facts while updating changed ones (errors concentrate on preferences and entity names), (c) >93% of failures stem from memory retrieval rather than response generation — independent support for EvoEmbedding (arxiv:2606.21649) thesis that retrieval layer has the most leverage

Connect the Dots: Training LLMs for Long-Lifecycle Agents (Yanxi Chen, Weijie Shi, Yuexiang Xie, Boyi Hu, Yaliang Li, Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou — Alibaba) — End-to-end RL recipe trains base LLM with two-phase rollouts (task-solving + context-updating) and GRPO variant with fine-grained credit assignment; meta-capability for long-lifecycle agent deployment baked into weights rather than wrapped post-hoc; custom environments engineered to isolate meta-skill from domain skill; reports cross-domain generalization plus transfer from Connect the Dots scenarios to Ralph-loop settings; code released on GitHub; marked work-in-progress

GateMem: Benchmarking Memory Governance in Multi-Principal Shared-Memory Agents (Zhe Ren, Yibo Yang, Yimeng Chen, Zijun Zhao, Benshuo Fu, Zhihao Shu, Bingjie Zhang, Yangyang Xu, Dandan Guo, Shuicheng Yan) — First benchmark assuming multiple users share common memory pools (medical / office / education / household); jointly evaluates utility (long-horizon recall under state updates) + access control (authorization across roles) + active forgetting (reliable deletion on request); headline finding: no method simultaneously achieves strong utility + robust access control + reliable forgetting; long-context wins governance at high compute cost; retrieval/external-memory reduces cost but still leaks unauthorized or deleted information; code + dataset released on GitHub + HuggingFace

VibeThinker-3B: Exploring the Frontier of Verifiable Reasoning in Small Language Models (WeiboAI) — 3B dense reasoning model trained via Spectrum-to-Signal post-training (curriculum SFT + multi-domain RL + offline self-distillation); reports AIME26 94.3 / 97.1 with TTS, LiveCodeBench v6 80.2 Pass@1, LeetCode 96.1% acceptance on unseen, IFEval 93.4; claims match/exceed DeepSeek V3.2 + GLM-5 + Gemini 3 Pro at orders-of-magnitude smaller scale; proposes Parametric Compression-Coverage Hypothesis (verifiable reasoning compresses into small models, general knowledge requires broader parameter coverage); model availability not specified in abstract

OpenAI Codex Record & Replay (2026-06-18 product launch) — macOS-only feature observing user GUI workflow + window content during recording; Codex inspects captured workflow and drafts reusable Skill with use conditions + inputs + steps + verification criteria; Skill becomes reusable context for subsequent Codex tasks executing against Computer Use + browser actions + connected plugins; teams share recorded skills broadly; requires Computer Use enabled; initial availability excludes EEA/UK/Switzerland; first production-deployed implementation of demonstration-to-skill induction at general-purpose scope — sidesteps SKILL.md auto-mining failure mode by keeping human in demonstration loop and LLM drafting Skill text rather than learning policy

Recall: Local project memory for Claude Code (Raiyan Yahya — HN front page 2026-06-21, 96 points) — Claude Code plugin capturing session activity (prompts/responses/files/commands) into append-only .recall/history.md; regenerates .recall/context.md (1-2K-token compact digest: goal + status + next steps + recent git info) via deterministic TF-IDF + TextRank summarization — no LLM API call, no network, no token cost; surfaces prior context on session start with resume prompt; fences context.md as untrusted reference data; MIT-licensed; Python stdlib core with NumPy optional; distributed via Claude Code plugin marketplace; episodic memory pattern that avoids consolidation-decay failure mode by trading retrieval recall for monotonic correctness

Anthropic Claude Code v2.1.183 (2026-06-19) + v2.1.185 (2026-06-21) + Enterprise-Managed MCP Authorization (2026-06-18 beta) — v2.1.183 hardens auto mode by blocking destructive git and infrastructure commands before they fire + adds explicit model-deprecation warnings + /config help; v2.1.185 increases stream-stall retry threshold from 10s to 20s of silence + improves messaging to distinguish thinking from stalled (eliminates spurious retries in scheduled autonomous routines); Enterprise MCP authorization via Okta provides centrally-administrable MCP connector provisioning with zero-touch first-login across Claude chat + Claude Code + Cowork; first vendor-supplied guardrail for long-running autonomous Claude Code loops

Think Again or Think Longer? Selective Verification for Budget-Aware Reasoning (Sajib Acharjee Dip, Dawei Zhou, Liqing Zhang) — SEVRA (Selective Verification for Reasoning Allocation) decides per-example whether to verify initial answer or accept; diagnoses extra reasoning as non-uniformly valuable (repairs failures + wastes compute on correct answers + introduces harmful answer changes via verifier-induced regression); MATH-500 76.3% accuracy at -26.8% post-generation tokens; GSM8K transfer verifies only 3% of examples improving 93.4% → 94.5% accuracy at -91.2% verification tokens; recommendation: tune initial reasoning budget first then apply selective recovery only when explicit checks/bounded retries/auditability/regression-risk control matter

Apertus Mini (Andrei Panferov, Davit Melikidze, Martin Jaggi, Dan Alistarh — Swiss AI Initiative, released 2026-06-15) — Distilled Apertus-v1.1 family up to 4B parameters trained on 1.7T permissive-license tokens via pre-training distillation from Apertus-8B teacher logits; 24 new checkpoints (3 base + 3 instruct + 8 NVIDIA-quantized + 10 Apple-device-quantized) using Quantization-Aware Distillation (QAD) as short recovery stage on fully-trained models; first multi-billion-parameter open model family explicitly distilled-and-quantized for Apple Silicon rather than post-hoc converted; cost <20% of teacher training; HN re-surfaced 2026-06-21

UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents (Chakrabarti, Limpus, Rana, Bao, Tiwari, Crepaldi, Sirasao — AMD + UCLA + Purdue) — Walsh-Hadamard rotation + codebook quantization with asymmetric K/V treatment and AMD-specific decode-attention kernels anchored against FP8 KV baseline; 3.47x P50 TTFT in cache-pressured late rounds, 2.3x TTFT across all rounds, 1.63x output throughput; framed for multi-round context-heavy agent workflows

Execution-State Capsules / FlashRT (Liang Su) — Graph-bound checkpoint and restore mechanism for complete restorable execution state (KV caches + recurrent states + convolution states + metadata); FlashRT runtime supports snapshot, restore, fork, rollback at committed boundaries; tested RTX 5090, Jetson AGX Thor, DGX Spark; TTFT speedup 3.9x at 2K tokens to 27x at 16K tokens; sub-millisecond snapshot/restore on GPU-resident state; targets low-latency small-batch on-device interactive AI agents / speech / robot policies

WUPHF (nex-crm YC S26) — Go + React multi-agent collaborative office with dual memory (per-agent private notebooks + shared git-native markdown wiki); push-driven broker eliminates idle polling; per-agent MCP scoping (4 tools DM / 27 full office); claimed 97% Claude prompt-cache hit rate + flat ~40k billed tokens/turn across 10 turns vs traditional orchestrators growing 124k to 484k over 8 turns; wiki has entity-fact typed triplets, append-only audit logs, archivist-identity LLM-synthesized briefs, /lookup cited-answer retrieval, /lint contradiction detection; multi-LLM support including Ollama; Sustainable Use License

Marginal Advantage Accumulation / MAA (Mingyu Yang, Keye Zheng, Congchao Cheng, Yujie Liu, Xingkang Lu, Fan Jiang, Yefei Zheng) — Memory-driven agent self-evolution; diagnoses that batch-style trace distillation gives conflicting feedback to same memory operations across batches; constructs differential signals comparable across batches and accumulates signed evidence per operation via EMA with semantic identity merging; post-processing layer on top of existing memory systems; best in 14/16 settings across 4 benchmarks x 4 target models; ~75% optimization-phase token reduction vs online alternatives; fourth distinct memory-self-evolution mechanism in five days

Contagion Networks: Evaluator Bias Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems (Zewen Liu) — Formal framework for measuring systematic evaluator bias spread through multi-agent networks; three DeepSeek-chat agents with structured / balanced / evidence-based evaluation approaches; homogeneous contagion coefficients 0.157-0.352 vs cross-model 0.85-1.3 (3-5x stronger); expanding evaluator committee 1 to 3 cuts contagion 72.4%; three propagation regimes identified via spectral radius; 20 pages 4 figures 4 tables; code released

How Transparent is DiffusionGemma? (Joshua Engels, Callum McDougall, Bilal Chughtai, Janos Kramar, Senthoran Rajamanoharan, Cindy Wu, Arthur Conmy, Asic Q. Chen, Jean Tarbouriech, Min Ma, Brendan O'Donoghue, Joao Gabriel Lopes de Oliveira, Rohin Shah, Neel Nanda — Google DeepMind interpretability team) — Decomposes transparency into variable transparency (intermediate computational states) + algorithmic transparency (reasoning reconstruction); DiffusionGemma opaque serial depth 28.6x Gemma 4 by default; interpretable token bottleneck brings ratio to 1.1x with no downstream-task performance loss; identifies diffusion-specific phenomena (non-chronological reasoning, token/sequence smearing, intermediate-context reasoning)

When Does Streaming Tool Use Help? Characterizing Tool-Intent Stabilization in Streaming RAG (Elroy Galbraith) — Frames speculative-fire-on-partial-query as tool-intent stabilization; CRAG benchmark 1371 validation questions; at realistic operating point (L=600ms, delta=3w/s, theta=0.8): 73.9% of queries admit substantial latency hiding; 21.3% have verbatim-present gold evidence; 95.2% streamability on favorable slice; Kruskal-Wallis p=0.017 epsilon-squared=0.04 for question-type effects

Multi-LCB: Extending LiveCodeBench to Multiple Programming Languages (Maria Ivanova, Pavel Zadorozhny, Rodion Levichev, Ivan Petrov, Adamenko Pavel, Ivan Lopatin, Alexey Kutalev, Dmitrii Babaev; ICLR 2026) — Extends LiveCodeBench from Python-only to 12 additional programming languages by translating tasks while preserving contamination controls; auto-tracks upstream LCB feed; evaluates 24 LLMs; finds Python overfitting + language-specific contamination + substantial cross-language disparities

LedgerAgent: Structured State for Policy-Adherent Tool-Calling Agents (Md Nayem Uddin, Amir Saeidi, Eduardo Blanco, Chitta Baral) — Inference-time wrapper maintains task state in a separate ledger rendered into the prompt; validates state-dependent policy constraints before environment-changing tool calls; improves average pass^k across four customer-service domains with largest gains under stricter multi-trial consistency metrics

Multi-Agent Transactive Memory (MATM, To Eun Kim, Xuhong He, Dishank Jain, Ambuj Agrawal, Negar Arabzadeh, Fernando Diaz) — Producer agents contribute completed task trajectories to a shared store; consumer agents retrieve them as procedural knowledge with no joint training or coordination protocol; reports improvements on ALFWorld and WebArena including reduced interaction steps; raw-trajectory pattern avoids LLM-consolidation step that triggers consolidation-decay

H-RePlan + HeraBench: Hierarchical Recovery for Cross-Device Agent Systems (Shu Yao, Yuhua Luo, Qian Long, Jingru Fan, Zhuoyuan Yu, Yuheng Wang, Lin Wu, Yufan Dang, Huatao Li, Chen Qian) — Separates device-local strategy recovery from orchestrator-level replanning via compact cross-layer failure abstraction; interchangeable execution strategies per device; HeraBench is fault-injected cross-device workflow benchmark on Linux + Android; higher completion / perfect-pass / lower token cost vs global-replan baselines

FAPO: Fully Autonomous Prompt Optimization of Multi-Step LLM Pipelines (Paul Kassianik, Baturay Saglam, Huaibo Zhao, Blaine Nelson, Supriti Vijay, Aman Priyanshu, Amin Karbasi, Cisco Foundation AI) — Pipeline-aware optimizer diagnoses retrieval/reasoning/formatting bottlenecks; prompt edits first, escalates to structural changes when attribution analysis flags architectural constraints; beats GEPA on 15/18 model-benchmark comparisons; mean +14.1 pp where ranges are non-overlapping; +33.8 pp mean on HoVer + IFBench (structural-change tasks); +2.0 to +7.1 pp on CTIBench-RCM security tasks

Is It Agentic Enough? Benchmarking Open Models on Your Own Tooling (HuggingFace) — Three-tier harness (Bare = pip-installed transformers / Clone = full repo source / Skill = packaged docs + task examples in context); large models (Kimi-K2.6, GLM-5.1, MiniMax-M2.7) reduce turns + time under CLI+Skill despite initial input-token spike; small models break catastrophically — Qwen3-14B collapses 100% → 0% on sentiment classification under Skill variant by treating CLI docs as executable tool; agent-facing APIs require capability-spectrum evaluation

Automating SKILL.md Generation for Computer-Using Agents via Interaction Trajectory Mining (Yuexing Hao, Xiaomin Li) — Three-stage pipeline (segment GUI trajectories → cluster into candidate skills → train skill-aware policies via GRPO); five of eight clusters reach ≥0.95 purity against InteraSkill Workflows labels; GRPO improves InteraSkill skill-step accuracy 18.5% → 20.5% only, negligible on BrowseComp+, and method underperforms trivial frequency priors on key source-domain metrics; framed as diagnostic — auto skill mining is interpretable but not yet reliable policy-improvement substrate; boundary detector / segment representation / offline reward model identified as bottlenecks

Securing the Future of AI Agents: AI Control Roadmap (Google DeepMind security + Gemini Spark teams, June 18 2026) — Defense-in-depth framework treating internal AI agents as potentially-misaligned insiders; MITRE ATT&CK-adapted threat modeling; trusted AI supervisors monitor agent reasoning/actions with pre-execution blocking; capability scaling tied to AI advancement levels; analyzed one million coding-agent trajectories finding most flagged events come from agent misinterpretation/overeagerness rather than adversarial intent; informed live monitoring for Gemini Spark; first public production-scale base rate on agent overreach vs. attack; two artifacts: AI Control Roadmap technical report + Three Layers of Agent Security policy framework

Reliability without Validity: A Systematic, Large-Scale Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge (Justin D. Norman, Michael U. Rivera, D. Alex Hughes) — 21 judges from 9 providers across MT-Bench / JudgeBench / RewardBench; 118 runs, ~541,000 individual judgments, three protocols (agreement, consistency, bias); universal 33–41 pp gap between exact-match agreement and Cohen's kappa on MT-Bench (most LLM-judge numbers chance-inflated); judge rankings shift up to 14 positions across benchmarks; consistency-bias paradox — two production judges show >0.95 test-retest reliability simultaneously with >0.10 position bias; verbosity bias minimal (<0.011) under single pairwise rubrics; proposes Minimum Viable Validation Protocol

DeepSeek-V4 (DeepSeek-AI, 319 authors, submitted by Wenfeng Liang) — Preview Release of MoE Pair Supporting 1M-Token Context; V4-Pro 1.6T Parameters / 49B Activated + V4-Flash 284B Parameters / 13B Activated; Three Architectural Innovations (Hybrid Attention Combining Compressed Sparse Attention + Heavily Compressed Attention / Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections / Muon Optimizer); 32T+ Pretraining Tokens with Full Post-Training; At 1M-Token Context vs V3.2 — 27% of Single-Token Inference FLOPs + 10% of KV Cache; Strongest Single-Paper Push on Long-Context KV-Cache Axis Since V3.2; Weights on Hugging Face deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4

AtomMem (Yao / S. Li / Z. Zheng / H. Zheng / Q. Liu / Xu / Chen) — Long-Term Memory System for LLM Agents via Atomic Facts; Four-Stage Pipeline (Fact Executor Extracts High-Value Atomic Facts → Hierarchical Event Structures → Temporal Profiles Tracking Dynamically Evolving User Attributes → Associative Memory Graph Activated at Retrieval); State-of-the-Art on LoCoMo Benchmark Across Reasoning Tasks; Fourth Per-User Memory Substrate in Five Days (vs UaC Typed Code / PreAct State-Machine Programs / Engram Parametric Hash-Keyed Edits); Stays in Context Tier But Adds Hierarchical-Event + Temporal-Profile Layer; 19 Pages 10 Figures 5 Tables

CacheWeaver (Tan / Gu / M. Li) — Cache-Aware Evidence Ordering for Grounded RAG; Diagnoses That Adjacent Queries Retrieve Overlapping Evidence in Different Orders So Set Overlap Doesn't Translate to Prefix Overlap; Prompt-Layer Scheduler (Engine + Retrieval Untouched) Maintains Prefix Tree Over Recently Served Evidence Sequences + Greedy Walk Places Most Reusable Prefix First; Across Three vLLM Configs — Median TTFT Down 20–33% vs Retrieval-Order Prefix Caching With No Quality Drop; Greedy Policy Reaches 97.5% of Oracle Ordering's Median TTFT Gain; Most Reusable Prefix Locality Recoverable by Simple Scheduling Without Changing Serving Engine

HydraHead (Tan / W. Chen / Shen / Y. Liu / X. Shen / Y. Wu / Ye) — Head-Axis Hybridization of Full Attention + Linear Attention Instead of Layer-Wise; Interpretability Analysis Shows Layers Block-Wise Functionally Similar But Individual Heads Within Same Layer Display Distinct Specialization; Two Innovations (Interpretability-Driven Selection Strategy Identifies Retrieval-Critical Heads Preserving FA Only for Them + Scale-Normalized Fusion Module Reconciles FA/LA Distributional Gap); Three-Stage Transfer Pipeline With Parameter Reuse + Distillation; Trained on Only 15B Tokens; +69% Over Baseline at 512K Context Length Approaching Qwen3.5 (256K Native) at Comparable Size; Matches 3:1 Layer-Wise Hybrid Performance at 7:1 LA-to-FA Ratio

Anthropic Frontier Red Team — Project Fetch: Phase Two (Ilie / Freeman / Troy, June 18, 2026); Claude Opus 4.7 Autonomously Controls Robotic Quadruped Through Code (Connects to Sensors / Writes Control Programs / Detects Objects); Three Trials With Adaptive Thinking at Maximum Effort in Claude Code; Human Involvement Limited to Laptop Setup + Initial Prompting + Task Approvals; ~20× Faster Than Fastest Human Team; On Four Shared Tasks — 37.7× Faster Than Non-Claude Humans + 18.9× Faster Than Claude-Assisted Humans + 1,045 LOC vs 10,309 LOC for Human-Claude Team at Equal-or-Better Results; Minimal Variance Across Three Trial Runs; Anthropic Explicitly Disclaims 'LLMs Have Solved Robotics' Framing (Closed-Loop Control Like Beach-Ball Retrieval Still Breaks); First Frontier-Model Robotics Win Not Going Through Behavior Cloning or Vision-Language-Action Model
